## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/r2/scripts/overlaycheck.py =====

```
"""Checks of the round-2 Loop overlay and of the retarget checks. Read-only.

Usage:
  python3 -I overlaycheck.py overlay <overlay.out> <baseline.out> <n prints>
      0 errors; 0 `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings; the warning multiset (message and the
      line after it, locations dropped) equal to the baseline's (the tip's Loop.lean
      elaborated alone); exactly <n prints> `#print axioms` results, none with `sorryAx` or an
      axiom other than propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
  python3 -I overlaycheck.py retarget <r2.lean> <r2.out> <tip.lean> <tip.out> <name> ...
      the r2 file has 0 errors; the tip file has errors exactly inside the examples restating
      the named copies (one or more errors each), and nowhere else.
  python3 -I overlaycheck.py diff <tip Loop.lean> <part1.lean> <added> <removed>
      the unified diff of part 1 against the tip adds and removes exactly the given numbers of
      lines, and every added line has at most 100 characters.
  python3 -I overlaycheck.py stmts <before.lean> <after.lean>
      declarations whose statement changed (cut at the proof's `:=`, bracket depth zero, not a
      `let`/`have` binder; docstrings and comments removed), added and removed declarations,
      and body-only changes: the private-statement-change list of the edit.
Each mode prints its findings and `RESULT: PASS` or `RESULT: FAIL`; exit code 0 or 1.
"""
import difflib
import re
import sys
from collections import Counter

STD = {'propext', 'Classical.choice', 'Quot.sound'}


def warnings(t):
    out, lines = [], t.split('\n')
    for i, l in enumerate(lines):
        m = re.match(r'^.*?\.lean:\d+:\d+: warning: (.*)$', l)
        if m:
            nxt = lines[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(lines) else ''
            out.append((m.group(1), nxt))
    return Counter(out)


def overlay(args):
    t, b, n = open(args[0], encoding='utf-8').read(), open(args[1], encoding='utf-8').read(), int(args[2])
    ok = True
    errs = len(re.findall(r'\.lean:\d+:\d+: error', t))
    sor = t.count("declaration uses 'sorry'")
    print(f'errors {errs}; sorry warnings {sor}')
    ok &= errs == 0 and sor == 0
    wa, wb = warnings(t), warnings(b)
    print(f'warnings {sum(wa.values())} (baseline {sum(wb.values())}); multiset equal: {wa == wb}')
    for k in (wa - wb):
        print('  extra warning:', k)
    for k in (wb - wa):
        print('  missing warning:', k)
    ok &= wa == wb
    items = re.findall(r"'([^']+)' (depends on axioms: \[([^\]]*)\]|does not depend on any axioms)",
                       t, re.S)
    bad = []
    for name, _, ax in items:
        axs = {a.strip() for a in ax.replace('\n', ' ').split(',') if a.strip()}
        flag = 'BAD' if axs - STD else 'ok '
        if axs - STD:
            bad.append(name)
        print(f'  {flag} {name}: {", ".join(sorted(axs)) or "(none)"}')
    print(f'axiom prints {len(items)} (expected {n}); with sorryAx or a nonstandard axiom: {bad}')
    ok &= len(items) == n and not bad
    return ok


def example_of(lean_lines, n):
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        m = re.match(r'^/-- Restates the copy (\S+) ', lean_lines[i])
        if m:
            return m.group(1)
        if lean_lines[i].startswith('/-! Retarget checks'):
            return None
    return None


def retarget(args):
    r2l, r2o, tl, to, names = args[0], args[1], args[2], args[3], set(args[4:])
    ok = True
    e2 = re.findall(r'\.lean:(\d+):\d+: error', open(r2o, encoding='utf-8').read())
    print(f'r2 file errors: {len(e2)}')
    ok &= not e2
    lines = open(tl, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
    et = [int(x) for x in re.findall(r'\.lean:(\d+):\d+: error', open(to, encoding='utf-8').read())]
    where = Counter(example_of(lines, n) for n in et)
    print(f'tip file errors: {len(et)}, by restated copy: {dict(where)}')
    ok &= set(where) == names
    return ok


def diff(args):
    a = open(args[0], encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
    b = open(args[1], encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
    d = list(difflib.unified_diff(a, b, lineterm=''))
    add = [l[1:] for l in d if l.startswith('+') and not l.startswith('+++')]
    rem = [l for l in d if l.startswith('-') and not l.startswith('---')]
    wide = [l for l in add if len(l) > 100]
    print(f'added {len(add)} (expected {args[2]}); removed {len(rem)} (expected {args[3]}); '
          f'added lines over 100 characters: {len(wide)}; hunks: {sum(1 for l in d if l.startswith("@@"))}')
    return len(add) == int(args[2]) and len(rem) == int(args[3]) and not wide


KW = r'(theorem|lemma|def|abbrev|instance|structure|inductive|class)'
DECL = re.compile(r'^(@\[[^\]]*\]\s*)*((private|protected|noncomputable|nonrec|partial|unsafe)\s+)*'
                  + KW + r'\s+([^\s(:{\[]+)')
LET = re.compile(r'\b(let|have)\s+[^\s:=()]+(\s*:[^=]*)?\s*$')


def strip(text):
    out, depth, i = [], 0, 0
    while i < len(text):
        if text.startswith('/-', i):
            depth += 1; i += 2; continue
        if depth and text.startswith('-/', i):
            depth -= 1; i += 2; continue
        if not depth and text.startswith('--', i):
            j = text.find('\n', i)
            i = len(text) if j < 0 else j
            continue
        if not depth:
            out.append(text[i])
        i += 1
    return ''.join(out)


def decls(path):
    lines = strip(open(path, encoding='utf-8').read()).split('\n')
    res, cur = {}, None
    for i, l in enumerate(lines + ['end']):
        m = DECL.match(l)
        top = m or re.match(r'^(end\b|namespace\b|section\b|open\b|variable\b|set_option\b|#|'
                            r'attribute\b|theorem|lemma|example)', l)
        if top and cur:
            res[cur[0]] = (cur[1], '\n'.join(lines[cur[2]:i]).strip())
            cur = None
        if m:
            cur = (m.group(5), 'private' in (m.group(2) or ''), i)
    return res


def stmt(code):
    depth = 0
    for i, ch in enumerate(code):
        if ch in '([{⟨':
            depth += 1
        elif ch in ')]}⟩':
            depth -= 1
        elif depth == 0 and code.startswith(':=', i) and not LET.search(code[:i]):
            return ' '.join(code[:i].split())
    return ' '.join(code.split())


def stmts(args):
    A, B = decls(args[0]), decls(args[1])
    changed = sorted(('private ' if A[n][0] else 'public ') + n for n in A if n in B
                     and stmt(A[n][1]) != stmt(B[n][1]))
    body = sorted(('private ' if A[n][0] else 'public ') + n for n in A if n in B
                  and stmt(A[n][1]) == stmt(B[n][1]) and ' '.join(A[n][1].split()) != ' '.join(B[n][1].split()))
    print(f'declarations before {len(A)}, after {len(B)}')
    print('added:', sorted(('private ' if B[n][0] else 'public ') + n for n in B if n not in A))
    print('removed:', sorted(n for n in A if n not in B))
    print('STATEMENT CHANGED:', changed)
    print('body-only changes:', body)
    return True


if __name__ == '__main__':
    ok = {'overlay': overlay, 'retarget': retarget, 'diff': diff, 'stmts': stmts}[sys.argv[1]](sys.argv[2:])
    print('RESULT:', 'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL')
    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
```

## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/r2/scripts/retarget_checks.py =====

```
"""MIG-1 statement gate, round 2: Lean checks of the non-verbatim retargets in the Loop home.

Usage: python3 -I retarget_checks.py <worktree> <deletion-plan.json> <overlay part1.lean> <outdir>

For every region copy whose source is in `Build/Loop.lean` and whose code is not identical to its
source (the old-host phase lemmas: modified and statement-identical copies), the copy's statement
(comment-stripped, region names unprefixed, `private lemma f2_X` -> `example`) is restated and
proved from the retarget in one step: `apply X (forward := false) <;> assumption` (`(pre := [])`
added where the source has an output-prefix parameter), `apply X <;> assumption` where the source
has no forwarding parameter. A restated copy that is stronger than its retarget fails. Also
restated: Catalog's `f2_head_steps`, proved from the MIG-0b stand-in by `Finset.mem_Icc.mp`.

Writes <outdir>/RetargetChecks-r2.lean (overlay part 1, the repaired Loop, then the examples) and
<outdir>/RetargetChecks-tip.lean (the tip's Loop verbatim, then the same examples except the head
example, whose stand-in the tip lacks): the negative control. Expected: the r2 file elaborates
without errors; the tip file fails exactly at two examples: `loopHost_prepare` (finding 1: the
original lacks the fuel-head clause) and `loopHost_contracts` (the original lacks the two head
clauses; the round-1 plan already replaces it by the moved copy). The moved contract's example
re-packs the explicit coefficient: `⟨10, loopHost_contracts …⟩`.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import region as RG  # noqa: E402
from decls import scan  # noqa: E402

WT, PLAN, PART1, OUT = sys.argv[1:5]


LET = re.compile(r'\b(let|have)\s+[^\s:=()]+(\s*:[^=]*)?\s*$')


def top_assign(text):
    """Index of the `:=` that opens the proof: the first one at bracket depth zero that does
    not bind a `let`/`have` inside the statement (`f2_loopHost_round` states `let start := …`)."""
    depth = 0
    for i, ch in enumerate(text):
        if ch in '([{⟨':
            depth += 1
        elif ch in ')]}⟩':
            depth -= 1
        elif depth == 0 and text.startswith(':=', i) and not LET.search(text[:i]):
            return i
    raise AssertionError(text[:200])


plan = json.load(open(PLAN, encoding='utf-8'))
rows = plan['rows']
names = {r['name'] for r in rows}
rmap = {n: RG.unprefix(n) for n in names if RG.unprefix(n)}
cat_path = os.path.join(WT, RG.CATALOG)
cat_code = RG.strip_comments(open(cat_path, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n'))
D, _ = scan(cat_path)
dl = {d['name']: d for d in D if plan['region'][0] < d['line'] < plan['region'][1]}
loop_path = os.path.join(WT, RG.HOMES['Loop'])
loop_code = RG.strip_comments(open(loop_path, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n'))
LD, _ = scan(loop_path)
ld = {d['line']: d for d in LD}


def wrap(line):
    """Break a statement line over 100 columns at a space inside parentheses (layout-neutral
    in a term), the continuation indented four more columns."""
    out = []
    while len(line) > 100:
        ind = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        depth, cut = 0, None
        for i, ch in enumerate(line):
            if ch in '([{⟨':
                depth += 1
            elif ch in ')]}⟩':
                depth -= 1
            elif ch == ' ' and depth > 0 and ind < i <= 98:
                cut = i
        assert cut is not None, line
        out.append(line[:cut])
        line = ' ' * (ind + 4) + line[cut + 1:]
    return out + [line]


def restated(name):
    code = '\n'.join(RG.rename(RG.code_of(cat_code, dl[name]), rmap))
    code = '\n'.join(w for l in code.split('\n') for w in wrap(l))
    stmt = code[:top_assign(code)].rstrip()
    first, rest = stmt.split('\n', 1)
    head = 'private lemma ' + RG.unprefix(name) + ' '
    assert first.startswith(head), first
    return '/-- Restates the copy ' + name + ' (statement only). -/\nexample ' + \
        first[len(head):] + '\n' + rest, code


examples, report = [], []
for r in rows:
    src = r.get('source') or ''
    if not src.startswith('Loop:') or r.get('code_identical') or r['kind'] != 'lemma':
        continue
    _, ln, base = src.split(':')
    scode = '\n'.join(RG.code_of(loop_code, ld[int(ln)]))
    sstmt = scode[:top_assign(scode)]
    named = ''
    if re.search(r'\((?:[^():]*\s)?forward(?:\s[^():]*)?\s*:\s*Bool\)', sstmt):
        named += ' (forward := false)'
    if '(pre : List Bool)' in sstmt:
        named += ' (pre := [])'
    text, _ = restated(r['name'])
    if r['name'] == 'f2_loopHost_contracts':
        # the moved contract is the copy with `∃ c` removed and `c ↦ 10`: re-pack the witness
        ex = text + ' :=\n  ⟨10, loopHost_contracts body F anchor Inv stepF acceptF out findMode s0 R T' \
            ' hF\n    hInv0 hInvStep hstart hround⟩\n'
        named = '⟨10, ·⟩ (the witness re-packed)'
    else:
        ex = text + ' := by\n  apply ' + base + named + ' <;> assumption\n'
    examples.append((r['name'], ex))
    report.append((r['name'], base, named.strip() or '(none)', r['fate']))

head_ex = restated('f2_head_steps')[0] + \
    ' :=\n  Finset.mem_Icc.mp (mig0bStandIn_workTapePos_runFrom_mem_Icc M c t i)\n'

hdr = ('\n/-! Retarget checks (MIG-1 round 2, not landed): each Loop-sourced non-identical copy\n'
       'of the Catalog region, restated, follows from its retarget in one step. -/\n\n'
       'namespace Turing.FinTM\n\n')
body = '\n'.join(ex for _, ex in examples)
part1 = open(PART1, encoding='utf-8').read()
tip = open(loop_path, encoding='utf-8').read()
r2 = part1.rstrip('\n') + '\n' + hdr + body + '\n' + head_ex + '\nend Turing.FinTM\n'
neg = tip.rstrip('\n') + '\n' + hdr + body + '\nend Turing.FinTM\n'
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
for fn, t in [('RetargetChecks-r2.lean', r2), ('RetargetChecks-tip.lean', neg)]:
    wide = [l for l in t.split('\n')[t[:t.index(hdr)].count('\n'):] if len(l) > 100]
    assert not wide, wide[:3]
    open(os.path.join(OUT, fn), 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(t)
with open(os.path.join(OUT, 'retarget-checks.tsv'), 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    f.write('copy\tretarget (Build/Loop.lean)\tnamed arguments\tround-2 fate\n')
    for row in report:
        f.write('\t'.join(row) + '\n')
    f.write('f2_head_steps\tworkTapePos_runFrom_mem_Icc (MIG-0b; stand-in)\tFinset.mem_Icc.mp\t'
            'delete: duplicates an existing public declaration\n')
print('examples:', len(examples) + 1, '(r2 file);', len(examples), '(tip file)')
for row in report:
    print('  ', row[0], '->', row[1], row[2])
```

## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/r2/scripts/retarget.py =====

```
"""MIG-1 statement gate, round 2: the systematic retarget check over the deletion plan.

Usage: python3 -I retarget.py <worktree> <deletion-plan.json> <unit.lean> <mig0b Finite.lean>
                              <retarget-checks.tsv> <out.tsv>

Read-only on its inputs; standard library only. For every region declaration whose fate moves it
into a home (`move*`) or absorbs it into a gated statement (`absorbed*`), and for every region
name its code cites (statement and proof; `region.py`'s `uses`), the row records the cited name's
round-2 fate, its retarget, where the retarget lives and whether it is private, and a statement
comparison:

* statements are comment-stripped, whitespace-normalized and cut at the `:=` that opens the
  proof (bracket depth zero, not the binder of a `let`/`have` inside the statement; round 1's
  `region.statement` cut `f2_loopHost_round` at its `let start :=`, which this repairs), with
  the region's prefix map (`f2_X -> X`, `catalog_redirectX -> redirectX`) and the moved-name map
  applied to the copy;
* classes: IDENTICAL; MOVES-WITH (the cited name moves to the same home under the moved-name
  map: the same text); GENERALIZATION (a named instantiation, checked by Lean in
  `checks/RetargetChecks-r2.lean`, or by the bridge probe for the duplicates of public lemmas);
  WEAKER; NOT-CARRIED (the citer's proof is replaced, not moved, so the citation does not reach
  the home); PROBLEM (the cited name is deleted without a retarget).
* accessibility: a private retarget must live in the citer's receiving home; a public one must
  be in the receiving home's import closure (`closure` below, from the `import` lines of the
  worktree and of its Mathlib package; MIG-0b's Finite counts as Finite, the decision-4 import
  of `Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin` in Simulation is recorded as a condition).

Prints the population, the class counts and every row that is not IDENTICAL or MOVES-WITH.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import region as RG  # noqa: E402
from decls import scan  # noqa: E402

WT, PLAN, UNIT, FINITE, CHECKS, OUT = sys.argv[1:7]
T = 'TCSlib.Complexity.'
MODS = {'Simulation': T + 'TuringMachine.Simulation', 'Composition': T + 'TuringMachine.Composition',
        'Wrappers': T + 'TuringMachine.Build.Wrappers', 'Encoding': T + 'TuringMachine.Encoding',
        'TimeConstructible': T + 'ClassP.TimeConstructible', 'Loop': T + 'TuringMachine.Build.Loop',
        'Primitives': T + 'TuringMachine.Build.Primitives',
        'Catalog': T + 'TuringMachine.Build.Catalog'}
HOME_OF_PATH = {'Build/Loop.lean': 'Loop', 'Build/Primitives.lean': 'Primitives',
                'Build/Wrappers.lean': 'Wrappers', 'ClassP/TimeConstructible.lean': 'TimeConstructible',
                'TuringMachine/Simulation.lean': 'Simulation'}
LET = re.compile(r'\b(let|have)\s+[^\s:=()]+(\s*:[^=]*)?\s*$')
ML = os.path.join(WT, '.lake/packages/mathlib')


def imports(mod):
    root = WT if mod.startswith('TCSlib') else ML if mod.startswith('Mathlib') else None
    if root is None:
        return []
    p = os.path.join(root, mod.replace('.', '/') + '.lean')
    if not os.path.isfile(p):
        return []
    return [l.split()[1] for l in open(p, encoding='utf-8') if l.startswith('import ')]


def closure(mod):
    seen, st = set(), [mod]
    while st:
        for y in imports(st.pop()):
            if y not in seen:
                seen.add(y)
                st.append(y)
    return seen


def statement(lines):
    text = '\n'.join(lines)
    depth = 0
    for i, ch in enumerate(text):
        if ch in '([{⟨':
            depth += 1
        elif ch in ')]}⟩':
            depth -= 1
        elif depth == 0 and text.startswith(':=', i) and not LET.search(text[:i]):
            return ' '.join(text[:i].split())
        elif depth == 0 and text.startswith(' where', i) and (i + 6 == len(text) or text[i + 6] in ' \n'):
            return ' '.join(text[:i].split())
    return ' '.join(text.split())


def body_stmt(st):
    """The statement without its keyword, modifiers and name (for comparisons across names)."""
    m = re.match(r'^(?:(?:private|protected|noncomputable)\s+)*(theorem|lemma|def|abbrev|instance|'
                 r'inductive|structure)\s+\S+\s*(.*)$', st)
    return (m.group(1), m.group(2)) if m else (None, st)


plan = json.load(open(PLAN, encoding='utf-8'))
rows = plan['rows']
by = {r['name']: r for r in rows}
names = set(by)
moved = {r['name']: r['new_name'].split('.')[-1] for r in rows if r.get('new_name')}
rmap = {n: RG.unprefix(n) for n in names if RG.unprefix(n)}
rmap.update(moved)
cat_path = os.path.join(WT, RG.CATALOG)
cat_code = RG.strip_comments(open(cat_path, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n'))
CD, _ = scan(cat_path)
cd = {d['name']: d for d in CD if plan['region'][0] < d['line'] < plan['region'][1]}
homes = {}
for k, rel in RG.HOMES.items():
    p = os.path.join(WT, rel)
    hd, _ = scan(p)
    homes[k] = (RG.strip_comments(open(p, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')), hd)
ucode = RG.strip_comments(open(UNIT, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n'))
UD, _ = scan(UNIT)
fcode = RG.strip_comments(open(FINITE, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n'))
FD, _ = scan(FINITE)
checked = {}
for l in open(CHECKS, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')[1:]:
    if l.strip():
        c = l.split('\t')
        checked[c[0]] = c[2]
clos = {k: closure(m) for k, m in MODS.items()}


def copy_stmt(n):
    return statement(RG.rename(RG.code_of(cat_code, cd[n]), rmap))


def home_stmt(k, line=None, name=None):
    code, hd = homes[k]
    d = [x for x in hd if (line and x['line'] == line) or (name and x['name'] == name)]
    assert len(d) == 1, (k, line, name)
    return statement(RG.code_of(code, d[0])), d[0]['private'], d[0]['line']


def unit_stmt(short):
    d = [x for x in UD if x['name'] == short]
    assert len(d) == 1, short
    return statement(RG.code_of(ucode, d[0])), d[0]['private']


def receiving(r):
    f = r['fate']
    if f.startswith('move: replaces'):
        return 'Loop', True
    if f.startswith('move (statement'):
        return 'Simulation', True
    if f.startswith('move'):
        return HOME_OF_PATH[r['detail'].split(' (')[0]], True
    if f.startswith('absorbed'):
        home = r['detail'].split('(')[1].split(';')[0].strip()
        carried = r['name'] in PROOF_MOVES
        return home, carried
    raise AssertionError(r['name'])


# absorbed declarations whose proofs move as the specs' proofs (round-1 pack, deletion plan)
PROOF_MOVES = {'f2_counter_space', 'f2_cond_space', 'f2_branch_space', 'f2_exists_loopFind_space',
               'f2_space_of_time'}
DUP = {  # duplicates of public declarations: (retarget, where, evidence)
    'f2_head_steps': ('Turing.MultiTapeTM.workTapePos_runFrom_mem_Icc', 'Finite (MIG-0b)',
                      'Lean: checks/RetargetChecks-r2.lean (Finset.mem_Icc.mp of the stand-in)'),
    'f2_sum_add': ('Fin.sum_univ_add', 'Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin',
                   'Lean: bridge probe (one public term)'),
    'a2_map_sum': ('Fin.sum_univ_add', 'Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin',
                   'Lean: bridge probe (one public term)'),
    'f2_catalogPair_inverse': ('Turing.eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode', 'Encoding',
                               'Lean: bridge probe (one public term, binders reordered)'),
    'f2_loop_input_run_le': ('Turing.MultiTapeTM.timed_input_bound', 'Deterministic',
                             'Lean: bridge probe (one public term)'),
}
DUP_MOD = {'Finite (MIG-0b)': T + 'TuringMachine.Finite', 'Encoding': MODS['Encoding'],
           'Deterministic': T + 'TuringMachine.Deterministic',
           'Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin': 'Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin'}

out = []
pop = [r for r in rows if r['fate'].startswith('move') or r['fate'].startswith('absorbed')]
for r in pop:
    home, carried = receiving(r)
    for u in r['uses']:
        q = by[u]
        f = q['fate']
        cls, retarget, where, acc, ev = '', '', '', '', ''
        if not carried:
            cls, ev = 'NOT-CARRIED', 'the citer\'s proof is replaced over the named witnesses'
            retarget = q.get('new_name') or (q['source'] or '').split(':')[-1] or u
            where, acc = '-', '-'
        elif f.startswith('move'):
            if f.startswith('move (statement'):
                retarget, qhome = u, 'Simulation'
            elif f.startswith('move: replaces'):
                retarget, qhome = 'loopHost_contracts', 'Loop'
            else:
                retarget, qhome = moved[u], HOME_OF_PATH[q['detail'].split(' (')[0]]
            priv = q['private']
            where = qhome + (' (private)' if priv else ' (public)')
            same = qhome == home
            acc = 'yes' if same or (not priv and MODS[qhome] in clos[home]) else 'NO'
            cls = 'MOVES-WITH' if same else 'IDENTICAL'
            ev = 'the same declaration text, renamed by the moved-name map'
            if f.startswith('move: replaces'):
                cls = 'GENERALIZATION'
                ev = ('the moved contract, ∃ c removed and c ↦ 10: '
                      'Lean, checks/RetargetChecks-r2.lean (⟨10, loopHost_contracts …⟩)')
        elif f.startswith('delete: duplicates'):
            retarget, dmod, ev = DUP[u]
            where = dmod + ' (public)'
            cond = ''
            if dmod.startswith('Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin'):
                ok = dmod in clos[home] or MODS['Simulation'] in clos[home] or home == 'Simulation'
                cond = ' after F-A\'s import in Simulation (decision 4)'
            else:
                ok = DUP_MOD[dmod] in clos[home]
            acc = ('yes' + cond) if ok else 'NO'
            cls = 'GENERALIZATION' if u == 'f2_head_steps' else 'IDENTICAL'
            if u == 'f2_catalogPair_inverse':
                cls = 'GENERALIZATION'
        elif f.startswith('absorbed'):
            gate = q['detail'].split(' (')[0].split('.')[-1]
            retarget = q['detail'].split(' (')[0]
            gs, gp = unit_stmt(gate)
            ghome = q['detail'].split('(')[1].split(';')[0].strip()
            where = ghome + (' (private)' if gp else ' (public)')
            acc = 'yes' if ghome == home or MODS[ghome] in clos[home] else 'NO'
            cs = copy_stmt(u)
            cls = 'IDENTICAL' if body_stmt(cs)[1] == body_stmt(gs)[1] else 'DIFFERS'
            ev = 'gated statement in the unit'
        elif q.get('source'):
            k, ln, base = q['source'].split(':')
            hs, hp, _ = home_stmt(k, line=int(ln))
            retarget = base
            where = k + (' (private)' if hp else ' (public)')
            acc = 'yes' if k == home or (not hp and MODS[k] in clos[home]) else 'NO'
            cs = copy_stmt(u)
            same = body_stmt(cs) == body_stmt(hs)
            if q.get('code_identical'):
                cls, ev = ('IDENTICAL', 'code-identical copy') if same else ('PROBLEM', 'code '
                                                                            'identical, statement not')
            elif same:
                cls, ev = 'IDENTICAL', 'statement-identical copy (proof differs)'
            elif u in checked:
                cls = 'GENERALIZATION'
                ev = 'Lean, checks/RetargetChecks-r2.lean: ' + checked[u]
                if u == 'f2_loopHost_prepare':
                    cls = 'WEAKER at the tip; GENERALIZATION after the round-2 repair'
                    ev += ('; the same example fails against the tip\'s Loop '
                           '(checks/RetargetChecks-tip.lean)')
            elif u == 'f2_loopHost':
                cls = 'GENERALIZATION'
                ev = ('definition: f2_loopHost body F anchor findMode = '
                      'loopHostM body F anchor false findMode by rfl (bridge probe)')
            else:
                cls, ev = 'DIFFERS', 'unclassified'
        elif q['family'] == 'public':
            retarget, where = u, 'Catalog (public)'
            acc = 'yes' if home == 'Catalog' else 'NO'
            cls, ev = 'PROBLEM', 'a Catalog row cited from a lower home'
        else:
            cls, ev = 'PROBLEM', 'cited name is deleted without a retarget: ' + f
        out.append([r['name'], r['fate'].split(' (')[0][:40], home, 'yes' if carried else 'no', u,
                    f[:60], retarget, where, cls, acc, ev])

with open(OUT, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as fh:
    fh.write('citer\tciter fate\treceiving home\tproof carried\tcited\tcited fate (round 2)\t'
             'retarget\tretarget home\tstatement class\taccessible\tevidence\n')
    for o in out:
        fh.write('\t'.join(o) + '\n')
from collections import Counter  # noqa: E402
print(f'population: {len(pop)} declarations ({Counter(r["fate"].split(":")[0].split(" (")[0] for r in pop)});'
      f' citations: {len(out)}')
print('classes:', dict(Counter(o[8] for o in out)))
print('accessible:', dict(Counter(o[9] for o in out)))
print('carried citations by class:', dict(Counter(o[8] for o in out if o[3] == 'yes')))
for o in out:
    if o[8] not in ('IDENTICAL', 'MOVES-WITH') or o[9] not in ('yes', '-'):
        print(' | '.join(o[i] for i in (0, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9)), '|', o[10][:90])
```

## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/r2/scripts/region_r2.py =====

```
"""MIG-1 deletion plan: classify every declaration of the `Build/Catalog.lean` region.

Usage: python3 -I region_r2.py <worktree> <outdir> <fates json>

Round 2 (MIG-1 statement gate): `region.py` of round 1 with two changes only, both asserted
edits: the fate manifest is an argument (round 2: `fates_r2.json`), and its `overrides`
section assigns a fate to a named declaration before the generic classification (round 2:
`f2_loopHost_prepare`, finding 1). Output and counts are otherwise computed as in round 1.

Read-only on the worktree; standard library only. Writes <outdir>/deletion-plan.json and
<outdir>/deletion-plan.tsv and prints the counts.

Method.
* Declarations: `decls.scan` (comment-aware scanner) of Catalog; the region is the
  `namespace Turing.FinTM` block between the first `f2_` docstring and its `end`.
* Code of a declaration: its lines from the keyword to the line before the next top-level
  command, comments and docstrings removed, trailing blanks dropped, each line right-stripped.
  "With docstrings" line counts add the immediately preceding docstring block.
* A copy's source: the declaration of the same name, after removing the prefix (`f2_`, or
  `catalog_redirect` -> `redirect`), in one of the seven home files.
* Code-identical: the copy's code with every region-local prefixed identifier renamed to its
  unprefixed form equals the source's code. Statement-identical: the same on the statement
  (the code up to the first top-level `:=` or `where`).
* Dependencies: identifier occurrences in code; closures run over region declarations.
* Fates follow the MIG-1 statement-gate plan (the pack, section "Deletion plan"): see FATE below.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from decls import scan  # noqa: E402

HOMES = {
    'Composition': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Composition.lean',
    'Primitives': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Primitives.lean',
    'Loop': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Loop.lean',
    'Wrappers': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Wrappers.lean',
    'TimeConstructible': 'TCSlib/Complexity/ClassP/TimeConstructible.lean',
    'Encoding': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Encoding.lean',
    'Simulation': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Simulation.lean',
}
CATALOG = 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Catalog.lean'
IDENT = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_'!?]*(?:\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_'!?]*)*")


def strip_comments(lines):
    out, depth = [], 0
    for s in lines:
        o, j = '', 0
        while j < len(s):
            if depth > 0:
                if s.startswith('/-', j):
                    depth += 1; j += 2; continue
                if s.startswith('-/', j):
                    depth -= 1; j += 2; continue
                j += 1; continue
            if s.startswith('/-', j):
                depth += 1; j += 2; continue
            if s.startswith('--', j):
                break
            o += s[j]; j += 1
        out.append(o.rstrip())
    return out


def doc_start(lines, line):
    s = line - 1
    j = s - 1
    while j >= 0 and lines[j].startswith('@['):
        j -= 1
    if j >= 0 and lines[j].rstrip().endswith('-/'):
        k = j
        while k >= 0 and not lines[k].lstrip().startswith('/--') and not lines[k].lstrip().startswith('/-'):
            k -= 1
        if k >= 0 and lines[k].lstrip().startswith('/--'):
            return k + 1
    return line


def code_of(code, d):
    c = code[d['line'] - 1:d['end']]
    while c and c[-1] == '':
        c.pop()
    return [l for l in c]


def statement(c):
    """Code up to the first top-level `:=` / ` where` (joined, whitespace-normalized)."""
    text = '\n'.join(c)
    depth = 0
    for i, ch in enumerate(text):
        if ch in '([{⟨':
            depth += 1
        elif ch in ')]}⟩':
            depth -= 1
        elif depth == 0 and text.startswith(':=', i):
            return ' '.join(text[:i].split())
        elif depth == 0 and text.startswith(' where', i) and (i + 6 == len(text) or text[i + 6] in ' \n'):
            return ' '.join(text[:i].split())
    return ' '.join(text.split())


def unprefix(name):
    if name.startswith('f2_'):
        return name[3:]
    if name.startswith('catalog_redirect'):
        return 'redirect' + name[len('catalog_redirect'):]
    return None


def rename(lines, mapping):
    def sub(m):
        tok = m.group(0)
        parts = tok.split('.')
        return '.'.join(mapping.get(p, p) for p in parts)
    return [IDENT.sub(sub, l) for l in lines]


def main():
    wt, out, fates_path = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    cat_lines = open(os.path.join(wt, CATALOG), encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
    cat_code = strip_comments(cat_lines)
    D, _ = scan(os.path.join(wt, CATALOG))
    first = min(d['line'] for d in D if d['name'].startswith('f2_'))
    start = max(i + 1 for i, l in enumerate(cat_lines[:first]) if l.startswith('namespace Turing.FinTM'))
    end = min(i + 1 for i, l in enumerate(cat_lines) if i + 1 > first and l.startswith('end Turing.FinTM'))
    region = [d for d in D if start < d['line'] < end]
    homes = {}
    for k, rel in HOMES.items():
        hl = open(os.path.join(wt, rel), encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
        hd, _ = scan(os.path.join(wt, rel))
        homes[k] = (hl, strip_comments(hl), hd)
    index = {}
    for k in HOMES:
        for d in homes[k][2]:
            index.setdefault(d['name'], (k, d))
    names = {d['name'] for d in region}
    rmap = {n: unprefix(n) for n in names if unprefix(n)}
    rows = []
    code = {}
    for d in region:
        c = code_of(cat_code, d)
        code[d['name']] = c
        ds = doc_start(cat_lines, d['line'])
        r = dict(name=d['name'], line=d['line'], end=d['end'], kind=d['kind'],
                 private=d['private'], lines=d['end'] - d['line'] + 1,
                 lines_doc=d['end'] - ds + 1)
        base = unprefix(d['name'])
        if d['name'].startswith('f2_'):
            r['family'] = 'f2'
        elif d['name'].startswith('a2_'):
            r['family'] = 'a2'
        elif d['name'].startswith('catalog_redirect'):
            r['family'] = 'catalog_redirect'
        elif not d['private']:
            r['family'] = 'public'
        else:
            r['family'] = 'other-private'
        r['source'] = None
        if base and base in index:
            k, sd = index[base]
            hc = code_of(homes[k][1], sd)
            mine = rename(c, rmap)
            r['source'] = f"{k}:{sd['line']}:{base}"
            r['code_identical'] = [l.strip() for l in mine if l.strip()] == [l.strip() for l in hc if l.strip()]
            r['statement_identical'] = statement(mine) == statement(hc)
        rows.append(r)
    # dependencies inside the region
    uses = {}
    for r in rows:
        toks = set()
        for l in code[r['name']]:
            for t in IDENT.findall(l):
                toks.update(t.split('.'))
        uses[r['name']] = sorted(t for t in toks if t in names and t != r['name'])
    # instances are used implicitly: attach each instance to the inductive it is about
    for r in rows:
        if r['kind'] == 'instance':
            for t in uses[r['name']]:
                if t in names:
                    uses.setdefault(t, [])
                    if r['name'] not in uses[t]:
                        uses[t] = sorted(uses[t] + [r['name']])
    for r in rows:
        r['uses'] = uses[r['name']]
    by = {r['name']: r for r in rows}

    def leaf(n):
        r = by[n]
        return r['source'] is not None  # a copy: the home original is used instead

    def closure(roots, through_copies=False):
        seen, todo = set(), list(roots)
        while todo:
            n = todo.pop()
            if n in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(n)
            if leaf(n) and n not in roots and not through_copies:
                continue
            todo.extend(uses[n])
        return seen

    plan = json.load(open(fates_path, encoding='utf-8'))
    overrides = plan.get('overrides', {})
    families = plan['moved_families']
    absorbed = plan['absorbed']
    duplicates = plan['duplicates']
    replaces = plan['replaces']
    publics = plan['publics']
    reach = {}
    for fam, spec in families.items():
        for n in closure(spec['roots']):
            reach.setdefault(n, []).append(fam)
    # reach from every public row through everything (to find dead declarations)
    pub_names = [r['name'] for r in rows if r['family'] == 'public']
    live_all = closure(pub_names, through_copies=True)
    sform = set(closure(plan['sform_roots'], through_copies=True))
    others = set()
    for p in pub_names:
        if p in plan['sform_roots']:
            continue
        others |= closure([p], through_copies=True)
    for r in rows:
        n = r['name']
        fams = reach.get(n, [])
        if n in overrides:
            r['fate'] = overrides[n]['fate']
            r['detail'] = overrides[n]['detail']
        elif r['family'] == 'public':
            r['fate'] = publics[n]['fate']
            r['detail'] = publics[n]['detail']
        elif n in absorbed:
            r['fate'] = 'absorbed into a gated public statement'
            r['detail'] = absorbed[n]
        elif n in replaces:
            r['fate'] = 'move: replaces the original (extended statement)'
            r['detail'] = replaces[n]
        elif n in duplicates:
            r['fate'] = 'delete: duplicates an existing public declaration'
            r['detail'] = duplicates[n]
        elif r['source'] is not None and r.get('code_identical'):
            r['fate'] = 'delete: copy, original used'
            r['detail'] = r['source']
        elif r['source'] is not None and r.get('statement_identical'):
            r['fate'] = 'delete: statement-identical copy (proof differs), original used'
            r['detail'] = r['source']
        elif r['source'] is not None:
            r['fate'] = 'delete: modified copy, citations re-targeted at the original'
            r['detail'] = r['source']
        elif fams:
            fam = fams[0]
            r['fate'] = 'move'
            r['detail'] = f"{families[fam]['home']} ({fam})"
        elif n not in live_all:
            r['fate'] = 'delete: dead (reached from no public declaration)'
            r['detail'] = ''
        elif n in sform and n not in others:
            r['fate'] = 'delete: reached only from the decision-loop S-form proof (dropped)'
            r['detail'] = ''
        else:
            r['fate'] = 'UNASSIGNED'
            r['detail'] = ''
        r['families'] = fams
    # declarations whose every user is deleted (and that no kept family reaches)
    users = {r['name']: [q['name'] for q in rows if r['name'] in q['uses']] for r in rows}
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for r in rows:
            if r['fate'] != 'UNASSIGNED':
                continue
            us = users[r['name']]
            if us and all(by[u]['fate'].startswith('delete') for u in us):
                r['fate'] = 'delete: used only by deleted declarations'
                r['detail'] = ', '.join(us)
                changed = True
    # proposed private names of the moved declarations (prefix dropped, `a2_map` -> `fwdMap`)
    ns_of = {'ClassP/TimeConstructible.lean': 'Complexity.'}
    special = plan.get('new_names', {})
    moved = {}
    for r in rows:
        if not r['fate'].startswith('move') or r['family'] == 'public':
            continue
        n = r['name']
        if n in special:
            new = special[n]
        elif n.startswith('a2_map'):
            new = 'fwdMap' + n[len('a2_map'):]
        elif n.startswith('a2_Map'):
            new = 'FwdMap' + n[len('a2_Map'):]
        else:
            new = n[3:] if n.startswith('f2_') else n
        home = families[r['families'][0]]['home'] if r['families'] else 'Build/Loop.lean'
        full = ns_of.get(home, 'Turing.FinTM.') + new
        r['new_name'] = full
        moved[full] = home.split('/')[-1][:-5]
    json.dump(moved, open(os.path.join(out, 'moved-names.json'), 'w'), indent=1)
    json.dump(dict(region=[start, end], rows=rows), open(os.path.join(out, 'deletion-plan.json'), 'w'),
              indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
    with open(os.path.join(out, 'deletion-plan.tsv'), 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write('line\tend\tname\tkind\tfamily\tlines\tlines_doc\tsource\tcode_identical\t'
                'statement_identical\tfate\tdetail\tnew_name\n')
        for r in rows:
            f.write('\t'.join(str(x) for x in [r['line'], r['end'], r['name'], r['kind'], r['family'],
                                              r['lines'], r['lines_doc'], r['source'] or '',
                                              r.get('code_identical', ''),
                                              r.get('statement_identical', ''), r['fate'],
                                              r['detail'], r.get('new_name', '')]) + '\n')
    # summary
    from collections import Counter, defaultdict
    print(f'region: lines {start}-{end} ({end - start + 1} lines); declarations {len(rows)}')
    c = Counter(r['family'] for r in rows)
    print('families:', dict(c))
    f2 = [r for r in rows if r['family'] == 'f2']
    print('f2 with same-named source:', sum(1 for r in f2 if r['source']),
          '; code-identical:', sum(1 for r in f2 if r.get('code_identical')),
          '(lines with docstrings', sum(r['lines_doc'] for r in f2 if r.get('code_identical')), ')',
          '; statement-identical only:', sum(1 for r in f2 if r['source'] and not r.get('code_identical')
                                              and r.get('statement_identical')),
          '; differing:', sum(1 for r in f2 if r['source'] and not r.get('statement_identical')),
          '; no source:', sum(1 for r in f2 if not r['source']))
    cr = [r for r in rows if r['family'] == 'catalog_redirect']
    print('catalog_redirect code-identical:', sum(1 for r in cr if r.get('code_identical')), 'of', len(cr))
    fc = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0])
    for r in rows:
        k = r['fate'] if r['fate'] != 'move' else 'move: ' + r['detail']
        fc[(r['family'], k)][0] += 1
        fc[(r['family'], k)][1] += r['lines_doc']
    for (fam, k), (n, l) in sorted(fc.items()):
        print(f'  {fam:17s} {k}: {n} decls, {l} lines with docstrings')
    print('UNASSIGNED:', [r['name'] for r in rows if r['fate'] == 'UNASSIGNED'])


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/r2/scripts/fatetable.py =====

```
"""The deletion plan's fate-count table (the pack's table), from deletion-plan.json. Read-only.

Usage: python3 -I fatetable.py <deletion-plan.json>

Groups the 378 region declarations by fate (moves by their family) and prints, per group, the
number of declarations and of docstring-inclusive lines, then the total. The last line is
`total: <declarations> declarations, <lines> lines`.
"""
import json
import sys
from collections import OrderedDict

rows = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8'))['rows']
ORDER = [
    ('delete: copy, original used', 'f2', 'Delete: `f2_` copy code-identical to its home source'),
    ('delete: copy, original used', 'catalog_redirect',
     'Delete: `catalog_redirect*` copies of Wrappers\' redirect family'),
    ('delete: statement-identical copy (proof differs), original used', None,
     'Delete: statement-identical copy, different proof'),
    ('delete: modified copy, citations re-targeted at the original', None,
     'Delete: modified copy, citations re-targeted at the original'),
    ("delete: its fuel-head clause is added to Loop's loopHost_prepare (strengthened in place)",
     None, 'Delete: `f2_loopHost_prepare`; its fuel-head clause is added to Loop\'s original'),
    ('delete: duplicates an existing public declaration', None,
     'Delete: duplicates a public declaration'),
    ('delete: dead (reached from no public declaration)', None, 'Delete: dead'),
    ('delete: used only by deleted declarations', None, 'Delete: used only by deleted'),
    ('delete: reached only from the decision-loop S-form proof (dropped)', None,
     'Delete: decision-loop S-form only (the `a2_` ledger)'),
    ('absorbed into a gated public statement', None, 'Absorbed into a gated statement'),
    ('move:Build/Primitives.lean (forwarding map)', None, 'Move: forwarding map -> Primitives'),
    ('move:Build/Primitives.lean (polynomial space)', None, 'Move: polynomial space -> Primitives'),
    ('move:ClassP/TimeConstructible.lean (counter space)', None,
     'Move: counter space -> TimeConstructible'),
    ('move:Build/Wrappers.lean (conditional ledger)', None, 'Move: conditional ledger -> Wrappers'),
    ('move:Build/Loop.lean (loop budget)', None, 'Move: loop budget -> Loop'),
    ('move: replaces the original (extended statement)', None,
     'Move, replacing the original: the extended `loopHost_contracts`'),
    ('move:Build/Primitives.lean (pair length)', None, 'Move: pair length -> Primitives'),
    ('corollary in place (statement and name unchanged; proof from the gated specs)', None,
     'Public: space rows, corollaries in place'),
    ('move (statement, name and proof unchanged)', None, 'Public: two rewind lemmas -> Simulation'),
]
groups = OrderedDict((label, [0, 0, []]) for _, _, label in ORDER)
seen = set()
for r in rows:
    key = r['fate'] if r['fate'] != 'move' else 'move:' + r['detail']
    for fate, fam, label in ORDER:
        if key == fate and (fam is None or r['family'] == fam):
            g = groups[label]
            g[0] += 1
            g[1] += r['lines_doc']
            g[2].append(r['name'])
            seen.add(r['name'])
            break
missing = [r['name'] for r in rows if r['name'] not in seen]
assert not missing, missing
for label, (n, l, ns) in groups.items():
    extra = f'  [{", ".join(ns)}]' if n <= 2 else ''
    print(f'{label} | {n} | {l:,}{extra}')
print(f'total: {sum(g[0] for g in groups.values())} declarations, '
      f'{sum(g[1] for g in groups.values()):,} lines')
```

## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/r2/scripts/rowtotals.py =====

```
"""Consumer totals per row, and the difference from a previous measurement. Read-only.

Usage: python3 -I rowtotals.py <consumer-names.json> <consumers.json> <previous consumers.json>

The 53 public machine-existential rows are the consumer names minus the six R3 rows, the two
rewind head lemmas, `redirectTM_spaceUsedByTape` and `timeConstructible_id`; the 34 home rows are
those of them homed outside Catalog. For each row: external code citations (count and files)
now and before, every citation site that is new or gone, and every docstring or comment mention
that is new or gone (consumers.py's `doc`). Prints the aggregate lines `rows53: <citations> in
<files> files`, `rows34: ...` and `doc mentions: ...` last.
"""
import json
import sys

names = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8'))
now = json.load(open(sys.argv[2], encoding='utf-8'))
old = json.load(open(sys.argv[3], encoding='utf-8'))
NOT_ROWS = {'transferTM_run', 'copyTM_run', 'clearTM_run', 'compareTM_run', 'incrementTM_run_succ',
            'incrementTM_run_overflow', 'rewind_scan_heads', 'rewind_heads',
            'redirectTM_spaceUsedByTape', 'timeConstructible_id'}
CAT = 'TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Catalog'
rows = [(h, n) for h, n in names if n not in NOT_ROWS]
home = [(h, n) for h, n in rows if h != CAT]
assert len(rows) == 53 and len(home) == 34, (len(rows), len(home))


def tot(db, sel):
    c = sum(n for _, s in sel for _, _, n in db[s]['external'])
    f = {m for _, s in sel for m, _, _ in db[s]['external']}
    return c, f


for h, n in names:
    a = {(m, l) for m, l, _ in now[n]['external']}
    b = {(m, l) for m, l, _ in old[n]['external']}
    ca = sum(k for _, _, k in now[n]['external'])
    cb = sum(k for _, _, k in old[n]['external'])
    mark = '' if (ca, len({m for m, _ in a})) == (cb, len({m for m, _ in b})) else '  CHANGED'
    print(f"{n}: declared {len(now[n]['declared'])}; external {ca} in {len({m for m, _ in a})} files"
          f" (before {cb} in {len({m for m, _ in b})}){mark}")
    for m, l in sorted(a - b):
        print(f'    new citation site: {m}:{l}')
    for m, l in sorted(b - a):
        print(f'    gone citation site: {m}:{l}')
    da = {(m, l) for m, l, _ in now[n]['doc']}
    db = {(m, l) for m, l, _ in old[n]['doc']}
    for m, l in sorted(da - db):
        print(f'    new docstring/comment mention: {m}:{l}')
    for m, l in sorted(db - da):
        print(f'    gone docstring/comment mention: {m}:{l}')
dn = sum(k for _, s in names for _, _, k in now[s]['doc'])
do = sum(k for _, s in names for _, _, k in old[s]['doc'])
for label, sel in [('rows53', rows), ('rows34', home)]:
    c, f = tot(now, sel)
    c0, f0 = tot(old, sel)
    print(f'{label}: {c} in {len(f)} files (before {c0} in {len(f0)}; new files: '
          f'{sorted(x.split(".", 2)[2] for x in f - f0)})')
print(f'doc mentions of the {len(names)} names: {dn} (before {do})')
```

## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/r2/scripts/r3check.py =====

```
"""Confirm the R3 retirement sites at a worktree. Read-only.

Usage: python3 -I r3check.py <worktree> <r3-retirement.tsv>

For every row of the retirement table: the declaration line (`declared at`) holds a declaration
of the row, and every listed site line mentions it (a code site in code, a docstring site in a
comment or docstring). Prints one OK/BAD line per site and the summary
`r3: <ok> sites confirmed, <bad> mismatches`; exit code = number of mismatches.
"""
import os
import re
import sys

wt, tsv = sys.argv[1:3]
base = os.path.join(wt, 'TCSlib/Complexity')
cache = {}


def line(rel, n):
    # table paths are relative to TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine (`Build/…`) or name it
    path = rel if rel.startswith('TuringMachine/') else 'TuringMachine/' + rel
    if path not in cache:
        cache[path] = open(os.path.join(base, path), encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
    return cache[path][n - 1]


ok = bad = 0
rows = [l.split('\t') for l in open(tsv, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')[1:] if l.strip()]
for r in rows:
    names = [n.strip() for n in r[0].split(',')]
    if r[1] != '-':
        rel, n = r[1].split(':')
        t = line(rel, int(n))
        good = any(re.search(r'\btheorem\s+' + re.escape(x) + r'\b', t) for x in names)
        print(('OK ' if good else 'BAD'), 'declared', r[1], names)
        ok, bad = ok + good, bad + (not good)
    rel, rest = r[3].split(':', 1)
    for n in [int(x.strip().lstrip(':')) for x in rest.split(',')]:
        t = line(rel, n)
        good = any(x in t for x in names)
        if r[4] == 'code':
            good = good and not t.lstrip().startswith(('--', '/-', '*', '`')) and \
                any(re.search(r'(?<![\w`])' + re.escape(x) + r'\b', t.split('--')[0]) for x in names)
        print(('OK ' if good else 'BAD'), r[4], f'{rel}:{n}', names)
        ok, bad = ok + good, bad + (not good)
print(f'r3: {ok} sites confirmed, {bad} mismatches')
sys.exit(bad)
```

## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/r2/scripts/srecords.py =====

```
"""Decision 2's records: for the eight citation specs proved at stage S, the batch from which each
is sorry-free. Read-only; a text scan, not a kernel check.

Usage: python3 -I srecords.py <unit.lean> <spec-probe tail.lean>

At S a citation spec's proof is its spec-probe proof (`MIG1Probe.spec_X`, with the probe's
`MIG1Probe.*` helpers it names). Its dependencies are the unit's declarations cited in that proof,
followed transitively through proved unit theorems (the four promotions are proved at S by their
unchanged home proofs and end the walk). A dependency that is still `sorry` at S is one of the 19
specs filled by F-A, F-B or F-C (the unit's 31 sorried statements minus the four promotions and
the eight); the spec is sorry-free from the last batch among its dependencies' batches.
"""
import re
import sys

unit = open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8').read()
tail = open(sys.argv[2], encoding='utf-8').read()


def chunks(t):
    out = {}
    for c in re.split(r'\n(?=(?:/--|theorem |def |abbrev |private |noncomputable |instance |lemma ))', t):
        m = re.match(r'(?:/--(?:.|\n)*?-/\n)?(?:private |noncomputable )*(theorem|def|abbrev|lemma|instance)'
                     r' (\S+)', c)
        if m:
            out[m.group(2).replace('_root_.Turing.FinTM.', '')] = (
                m.group(1), c[m.end():], bool(re.search(r':= by\n  sorry\b', c)))
    return out


U, P = chunks(unit), chunks(tail)
PROMOTIONS = {'prependTM_computes', 'incFixedTM_computes', 'pairValidTM_computes', 'pairExtractTM_computes'}
EIGHT = ['callTM_run', 'redirectTM_runFrom', 'polyUnaryTM_computes', 'pairLenCheckTM_computes',
         'stripLastTM_computes', 'splitSolveTM_computes', 'splitSolveTM_spaceUsed',
         'splitSolveWithTM_computes']
BATCH = {'F-A': {'branchTM_spaceUsed', 'idTM_computes', 'ifEqTM_computes', 'condTM_computes_iff',
                 'timedCondTM_computes', 'timedCondTM_spaceUsed', 'pairDiagTM_computes',
                 'lengthBitsTM_computes', 'lengthBitsTM_spaceUsed'},
         'F-C': {'loopHostTM_contracts', 'loopHostTM_decides', 'loopHostTM_finds',
                 'loopHostTM_spaceUsed_le_budget', 'emitLoopTM_computes'},
         'F-B': {'polyUnaryTM_spaceUsed', 'unaryTokenTM_computes', 'appendBitTM_computes',
                 'pairMapSndTM_computes', 'pairMapSndTM_spaceUsed'}}
ORDER = ['S', 'F-A', 'F-C', 'F-B']  # integration order F-A, F-C, F-B
sorried = {n for n, (_, _, s) in U.items() if s and not n.startswith('MIG1Gate')}
later = sorried - PROMOTIONS - set(EIGHT)
assert later == set().union(*BATCH.values()), sorted(later ^ set().union(*BATCH.values()))
helpers = {n: b for n, (_, b, _) in P.items() if n.startswith('MIG1Probe.') and not n.startswith('MIG1Probe.spec_')}


def proof(n):
    if n in EIGHT:
        b = P['MIG1Probe.spec_' + n][1]
        return b + ''.join(hb for h, hb in helpers.items() if h in b)
    return U[n][1]


def deps(n, seen):
    body, res = proof(n), set()
    for m in U:
        if m == n or m.startswith('MIG1Gate') or not re.search(r'(?<![\w.])' + re.escape(m) + r"(?![\w'])", body):
            continue
        if m in later:
            res.add(m)
        elif m not in seen and U[m][0] in ('theorem', 'lemma') and m not in PROMOTIONS:
            seen.add(m)
            res |= deps(m, seen)
    return res


print(f'unit sorried statements: {len(sorried)}; promotions: {len(PROMOTIONS)}; the eight: {len(EIGHT)}; '
      f'filled later: {len(later)}')
for n in EIGHT:
    d = deps(n, set())
    b = max((next(k for k, v in BATCH.items() if x in v) for x in d), key=ORDER.index, default='S')
    print(f'{n}: proof supplied at S; sorry dependencies {sorted(d) or "none"}; sorry-free from {b}')
```

## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/scripts/campaign_style_lint.py =====

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Mechanical policy.md conformance lint for the Arora-Barak Chapter 1 tree.

Checks the mechanically checkable slice of policy.md (sections 1-3) plus the
campaign's standing conventions, so external audit rounds can consume a
reported attestation instead of performing style review (epoch-1/epoch-2
practice; see AroraBarakChapter1Plan.md section 5).

  FAIL  - unambiguous policy violation; exit code 1.
  WARN  - needs a recorded justification (e.g. a file over the 1000-line
          threshold with an escalation on file); exit code 0.
  INFO  - context only.

Usage: python3 scripts/style_lint.py [subtree]   (default: TCSlib/Complexity)
"""

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SUBTREE = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else Path("TCSlib/Complexity")

SIZE_TARGET = 600     # policy section 1: target upper end
SIZE_THRESHOLD = 1000 # policy section 1: split unless positively justified

# Vendored files follow upstream style (policy section 2, Statement prose:
# exempt from the docstring-presence requirement, and frozen anyway).
VENDORED = {
    "TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Configuration.lean",
    "TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Deterministic.lean",
    # vendored from [AFM26] anthropics/formal-math 3sum-apsp (design §15b)
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Assigns.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Calls.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Compiler/CallFrames.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Compiler/Cells.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Compiler/Conditions.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Compiler/Dispatcher.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Compiler/Expressions.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Compiler/ProgramCode.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Compiler/Simulation.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Compiler/StartUp.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Compiler/StatementCode.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Compiler/WholeProgram.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Frames.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Lib/ArrayAt.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Lib/Copy.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Lib/CountSort.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Lib/Emod.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Lib/Logs.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Lib/Merge.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Lib/MergeSort.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Lib/NextPair.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Lib/Odometer.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Lib/Pass.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Lib/PowTable.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Lib/RadixPass.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Lib/Seg.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Lib/Sqrt.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Logic.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Regions.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Rules.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/RunsStayInLimits.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Syntax.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Light/Tactics.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Util/Basic.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Util/CountingSort.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Util/Index.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Util/List.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Util/Odometer.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/Util/StablePass.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/WordRAM/Basic.lean",
    "TCSlib/Programs/WordRAM/Steps.lean",
}

# Declaration kinds requiring statement prose (instances exempt per policy).
DOC_DECL_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(?:@\[[^\]]*\]\s*)*(?:noncomputable\s+)?(private\s+)?(?:noncomputable\s+)?"
    r"(theorem|lemma|def|structure|abbrev|inductive)\s+([A-Za-z0-9_.']+)"
)
ATTR_LINE_RE = re.compile(r"^@\[[^\]]*\]$")
SET_OPTIONS = [
    "set_option maxHeartbeats 0",
    "set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false",
    "set_option autoImplicit false",
]
DOCSTRING_RE = re.compile(r"/--.*?-/", re.S)
DECL_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(?:@\[[^\]]*\]\s*)?(?:noncomputable\s+)?(private\s+)?(?:noncomputable\s+)?"
    r"(theorem|def|lemma|structure|abbrev|instance|inductive)\s+([A-Za-z0-9_.']+)",
    re.M,
)

findings = []  # (level, path, message)


def note(level, path, msg):
    findings.append((level, str(path), msg))


def strip_comments(src: str) -> str:
    """Remove nesting-aware block comments (docstrings included) and line
    comments, so declaration counting never matches prose like `lemma advances`
    inside a docstring (epoch-2 audit, finding 3)."""
    out, i, depth = [], 0, 0
    while i < len(src):
        if src.startswith("/-", i):
            depth += 1
            i += 2
            continue
        if src.startswith("-/", i) and depth > 0:
            depth -= 1
            i += 2
            continue
        if depth == 0:
            out.append(src[i])
        i += 1
    return "\n".join(l.split("--")[0] for l in "".join(out).splitlines())


def is_facade(path: Path) -> bool:
    return (path.parent / path.stem).is_dir()


def check_file(path: Path):
    src = path.read_text()
    lines = src.splitlines()
    rel = path.relative_to(ROOT)

    # 1. Size (policy section 1).
    n = len(lines)
    if n > SIZE_THRESHOLD:
        note("WARN", rel, f"{n} lines > {SIZE_THRESHOLD}: policy requires a split "
                          "or a recorded justification (escalation/decision log)")
    elif n > SIZE_TARGET and not is_facade(path):
        note("INFO", rel, f"{n} lines > target {SIZE_TARGET}")

    # 2. Imports (policy section 1).
    if re.search(r"^import Mathlib$", src, re.M):
        note("FAIL", rel, "bare `import Mathlib`")

    # 3. References section (policy section 2) - math files and facades alike.
    if "## References" not in src and not is_facade(path):
        note("FAIL", rel, "module docstring lacks a `## References` section")

    # 4. Standard set_option header (campaign convention; facades exempt).
    if not is_facade(path):
        missing = [o for o in SET_OPTIONS if o not in src]
        if missing:
            note("WARN", rel, f"missing header option(s): {', '.join(missing)}")

    # 5. Every sorry is preceded by a docstring mentioning a proof sketch
    #    (policy section 3). Heuristic: nearest docstring above the sorry line.
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.strip() == "sorry":
            head = "\n".join(lines[:i])
            docs = DOCSTRING_RE.findall(head)
            if not docs or "sketch" not in docs[-1].lower():
                note("FAIL", rel, f"line {i + 1}: `sorry` without a proof sketch "
                                  "in the preceding docstring")

    # 6. Public/private declaration tally (INFO - context for audit packs).
    #    Counted on comment-stripped source (epoch-2 audit, finding 3).
    stripped = strip_comments(src)
    pub = sum(1 for m in DECL_RE.finditer(stripped) if not m.group(1))
    priv = sum(1 for m in DECL_RE.finditer(stripped) if m.group(1))
    note("INFO", rel, f"{n} lines; {pub} public / {priv} private declarations")

    # 7. Statement prose (policy section 2): every public declaration
    #    (instances and vendored files exempt) is immediately preceded by a
    #    docstring, skipping attribute / `open ... in` / `noncomputable` lines.
    #    Presence only; statement *quality* is review judgment.
    if str(rel) not in VENDORED:
        depth = 0
        for idx, line in enumerate(lines):
            if depth == 0:
                m = DOC_DECL_RE.match(line)
                if m and not m.group(1):
                    j = idx - 1
                    while j >= 0:
                        prev = lines[j].strip()
                        if (ATTR_LINE_RE.fullmatch(prev)
                                or (prev.startswith("open ") and prev.endswith(" in"))
                                or prev == "noncomputable"):
                            j -= 1
                            continue
                        break
                    if not (j >= 0 and lines[j].rstrip().endswith("-/")):
                        note("FAIL", rel,
                             f"line {idx + 1}: public {m.group(2)} "
                             f"`{m.group(3)}` has no preceding docstring "
                             "(policy section 2, statement prose)")
            depth += line.count("/-") - line.count("-/")


def check_facade(path: Path):
    """Every child .lean under the facade's directory must be imported."""
    src = path.read_text()
    rel = path.relative_to(ROOT)
    child_dir = path.parent / path.stem
    for child in sorted(child_dir.rglob("*.lean")):
        mod = ".".join(child.relative_to(ROOT).with_suffix("").parts)
        if not is_facade(child) and f"import {mod}" not in src:
            # A grandchild may legitimately be imported via its own facade.
            inter = child.parent / (child.parent.name + ".lean")
            covered = inter != path and inter.exists() and \
                f"import {'.'.join(inter.relative_to(ROOT).with_suffix('').parts)}" in src
            if not covered:
                note("FAIL", rel, f"facade does not import child module `{mod}`")


def main():
    files = sorted((ROOT / SUBTREE).rglob("*.lean"))
    if not files:
        print(f"no .lean files under {SUBTREE}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    for f in files:
        check_file(f)
        if is_facade(f):
            check_facade(f)

    width = max(len(p) for _, p, _ in findings)
    failed = False
    for level in ("FAIL", "WARN", "INFO"):
        for lv, p, msg in findings:
            if lv == level:
                print(f"{lv:4}  {p:<{width}}  {msg}")
                failed |= lv == "FAIL"
    print(f"\nstyle_lint: {sum(1 for l, _, _ in findings if l == 'FAIL')} FAIL, "
          f"{sum(1 for l, _, _ in findings if l == 'WARN')} WARN over {len(files)} files")
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/scripts/mkshim.py =====

```
"""Emit verbatim copies of declarations of one Lean file, in file order, with an identifier
rename applied (token level, dotted components renamed one by one). Read-only on the source.

Usage: python3 -I mkshim.py <file.lean> <rename.json|-> [--stmt] [--public] [--nodoc] <name> ...

With --stmt, every theorem/lemma body is replaced by `sorry` (statement shims; with --nodoc and
without --public a one-line shim docstring naming the source is added); with --public the
leading `private` is removed (and `lemma` becomes `theorem`); with --nodoc the preceding docstring is not copied (by default it
is).
"""
import json
import os
import re
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from decls import scan  # noqa: E402

IDENT = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_'!?]*(?:\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_'!?]*)*")


def rename_line(l, mapping):
    def sub(m):
        return '.'.join(mapping.get(p, p) for p in m.group(0).split('.'))
    # do not rename inside string literals or comments: the files have no string literals in
    # these declarations; comments are renamed too (docstrings name the declarations).
    return IDENT.sub(sub, l)


def stmt_cut(lines):
    """Index (line, col) of the `:=` that opens a theorem's proof: the first top-level `:= by`
    that ends a line, else the first top-level `:=` (a statement may contain `let x := e`)."""
    depth = 0
    for i, l in enumerate(lines):
        for j in range(len(l)):
            ch = l[j]
            if ch in '([{⟨':
                depth += 1
            elif ch in ')]}⟩':
                depth -= 1
            elif depth == 0 and l.startswith(':= by', j) and l[j + 5:].strip() == '':
                return i, j
    depth = 0
    for i, l in enumerate(lines):
        j = 0
        while j < len(l):
            ch = l[j]
            if ch in '([{⟨':
                depth += 1
            elif ch in ')]}⟩':
                depth -= 1
            elif depth == 0 and l.startswith(':=', j):
                return i, j
            j += 1
    raise ValueError('no :=')


def main():
    path, rmap = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    args = sys.argv[3:]
    stmt = public = nodoc = False
    while args and args[0].startswith('--'):
        flag = args.pop(0)
        if flag == '--stmt':
            stmt = True
        elif flag == '--public':
            public = True
        elif flag == '--nodoc':
            nodoc = True
        else:
            raise SystemExit(f'unknown flag {flag}')
    mapping = {} if rmap == '-' else json.load(open(rmap, encoding='utf-8'))
    ds, lines = scan(path)
    want = set(args)
    found = set()
    out = []
    for d in sorted(ds, key=lambda d: d['line']):
        if d['name'] not in want:
            continue
        found.add(d['name'])
        s = d['line'] - 1
        j = s - 1
        if j >= 0 and lines[j].rstrip().endswith('-/') and not nodoc:
            k = j
            while k >= 0 and not lines[k].lstrip().startswith('/--'):
                k -= 1
            if k >= 0:
                s = k
        body = lines[s:d['end']]
        while body and body[-1].strip() == '':
            body.pop()
        if public:
            off = d['line'] - 1 - s
            if body[off].startswith('private '):
                body[off] = body[off][len('private '):]
            if body[off].startswith('lemma '):
                body[off] = 'theorem ' + body[off][len('lemma '):]
        if stmt and d['kind'] in ('theorem', 'lemma'):
            off = d['line'] - 1 - s
            i, c = stmt_cut(body[off:])
            i += off
            body = body[:i] + [body[i][:c] + ':= by', '  sorry']
            if nodoc and not public:
                body = [f"/-- Statement shim of `{d['name']}` (`{os.path.basename(path)}:"
                        f"{d['line']}`), proved in the tree.", "**Proof sketch.** See the source. -/"] + body
        out.append('\n'.join(rename_line(l, mapping) for l in body))
    missing = want - found
    if missing:
        raise SystemExit(f'not found: {sorted(missing)}')
    print('\n\n'.join(out))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/scripts/decls.py =====

```
import re, sys, json
# List declarations of a Lean file: (start line, end line, kind, private, name)
KW = r'(theorem|lemma|def|abbrev|structure|inductive|instance|class)'
pat = re.compile(r'^(?:@\[[^\]]*\]\s*)?((?:private|protected|noncomputable|nonrec|partial|unsafe)\s+)*' + KW + r'\s+([^\s:({\[]+)?')
def scan(path):
    lines = open(path, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
    # strip comment blocks: track nesting for /- -/
    depth = 0
    starts = []
    code_flags = []
    for i, l in enumerate(lines):
        s = l
        out = ''
        j = 0
        while j < len(s):
            if depth > 0:
                if s.startswith('/-', j): depth += 1; j += 2; continue
                if s.startswith('-/', j): depth -= 1; j += 2; continue
                j += 1; continue
            if s.startswith('/-', j): depth += 1; j += 2; continue
            if s.startswith('--', j): break
            out += s[j]; j += 1
        code_flags.append(out)
        m = pat.match(out)
        if m and not out.startswith(' '):
            pre = out[:m.start(2)]
            starts.append((i + 1, m.group(2), 'private' in pre, m.group(3) or '', out.strip()))
    res = []
    n = len(lines)
    # end line: line before next decl start / next top-level docstring / namespace/end/section
    toplevel = set()
    for i, l in enumerate(lines):
        if re.match(r'^(/--|/-!|namespace |end |section|variable|open |set_option|@\[|private |theorem|lemma|def |abbrev|structure|inductive|instance|noncomputable|protected|attribute)', l):
            toplevel.add(i + 1)
    tl = sorted(toplevel)
    import bisect
    for (ln, kind, priv, name, text) in starts:
        k = bisect.bisect_right(tl, ln)
        end = (tl[k] - 1) if k < len(tl) else n
        # trim trailing blank lines
        while end > ln and lines[end - 1].strip() == '':
            end -= 1
        res.append(dict(line=ln, end=end, kind=kind, private=priv, name=name, head=text[:160]))
    return res, lines
if __name__ == '__main__':
    r, _ = scan(sys.argv[1])
    json.dump(r, open(sys.argv[2], 'w'), indent=0)
    print(len(r))
```

{
 "Prim": {
