## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/scripts/cutcheck.py =====

```
"""Cut check for a gate elaboration unit (read-only; standard library only).

Usage: python3 -I cutcheck.py <unit.lean> <worktree> <outdir>

The unit is split into parts at header lines starting with HEADER. Each part names its landing
module (`-- @landing M`) and its imports (`-- @imports a b ...`, possibly several lines). The
part's body is everything after its last `-- @imports` line up to the next header.

For every part P this writes <outdir>/<M>.check.lean: the copyright block, the imports of P's
import closure that exist in the worktree, the standard options, and the bodies of the parts in
P's closure (P and every part whose landing module P imports, transitively), in file order. An
import that names an existing module and also the landing module of a part (a local modification
of a vendored file) both imports the module and pulls in the part. It also reports whether the
unit's own imports are exactly the union of the existing imports that the parts list.
"""
import os
import sys

HEADER = "/-! ════"
COPYRIGHT = """/-
Copyright (c) 2026 Seyoon Ragavan. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
"""
OPTIONS = """set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false
"""


def exists(wt, mod):
    rel = os.path.join(*mod.split(".")) + ".lean"
    if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(wt, rel)):
        return True
    pk = os.path.join(wt, ".lake", "packages")
    return any(os.path.isfile(os.path.join(pk, d, rel)) for d in os.listdir(pk))


def main():
    unit, wt, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
    lines = open(unit, encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n")
    first_doc = next(i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith("/-!"))
    head_imports = [l.split()[1] for l in lines[:first_doc] if l.startswith("import ")]
    starts = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith(HEADER)]
    parts = []
    for n, s in enumerate(starts):
        e = starts[n + 1] if n + 1 < len(starts) else len(lines)
        block = lines[s:e]
        land = [l.split()[2] for l in block if l.startswith("-- @landing ")]
        imps = [w for l in block if l.startswith("-- @imports ") for w in l.split()[2:]]
        last = max(i for i, l in enumerate(block) if l.startswith("-- @imports "))
        assert len(land) == 1, f"part at line {s + 1}: one @landing line expected"
        parts.append({"land": land[0], "imports": imps, "body": block[last + 1:], "line": s + 1})
    by_land = {}
    for k, p in enumerate(parts):
        by_land.setdefault(p["land"], []).append(k)
    union = []
    for p in parts:
        for m in p["imports"]:
            if exists(wt, m) and m not in union:
                union.append(m)
    missing_head = [m for m in union if m not in head_imports]
    extra_head = [m for m in head_imports if m not in union]
    print(f"unit imports: {len(head_imports)}; union of part imports: {len(union)}; "
          f"missing from unit: {missing_head}; extra in unit: {extra_head}")
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    for k, p in enumerate(parts):
        closure, todo = set(), [k]
        while todo:
            j = todo.pop()
            if j in closure:
                continue
            closure.add(j)
            for m in parts[j]["imports"]:
                for i in by_land.get(m, []):
                    if i < j:
                        todo.append(i)
        order = sorted(closure)
        imps = []
        for j in order:
            for m in parts[j]["imports"]:
                if exists(wt, m) and m not in imps:
                    imps.append(m)
                elif not exists(wt, m) and m not in by_land:
                    raise SystemExit(f"part {p['land']}: import {m} is neither existing nor a part")
        name = p["land"] + (f".part{k}" if len(by_land[p["land"]]) > 1 else "")
        path = os.path.join(out, name + ".check.lean")
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(COPYRIGHT)
            f.write("".join(f"import {m}\n" for m in imps))
            f.write("\n" + OPTIONS + "\n")
            for j in order:
                f.write("\n".join(parts[j]["body"]).rstrip("\n") + "\n\n")
        labels = ", ".join(parts[j]["land"].split(".")[-1] + f"@{parts[j]['line']}" for j in order)
        print(f"{name}: closure [{labels}]; imports {imps}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/scripts/identity.py =====

```
"""MIG-1 statement gate: code identity of the gate unit against the library sources.

Usage: python3 -I identity.py <worktree> <unit.lean> <manifest.json> [<more unit files> ...]

Read-only; standard library only. Declarations are located with scripts/decls.py in the source
file and in the unit (by name; a name must occur once in the unit). Comments and docstrings are
removed and all whitespace is collapsed before comparing. `private` is dropped and `lemma` is
read as `theorem` on both sides, so that a promotion (private -> public, same text) compares
equal. The rename map named by an entry (scripts/renames.json) is applied to the source text
token by token. Kinds:

* verbatim   -- the whole declaration (statement and body) is identical.
* statement  -- the statements (up to the `:=` opening the proof) are identical, and the gate
                body is `by sorry` (a sorried spec stated verbatim from a proved private lemma).
* transform  -- as `statement`, after the listed literal substitutions on the source statement.
* binders    -- the gate statement's binders (before its statement colon) equal the source's
                (after the listed substitutions); the conclusions are new.
* substrings -- every nonblank line of the gate declaration's body occurs, whitespace-collapsed,
                as a substring of the source declaration, except the lines listed as `allow`.

Every entry prints PASS or FAIL with the reason; the exit code is the number of failures.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
from decls import scan  # noqa: E402

FILES = {
    'Composition': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Composition.lean',
    'Primitives': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Primitives.lean',
    'Loop': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Loop.lean',
    'Wrappers': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Wrappers.lean',
    'TimeConstructible': 'TCSlib/Complexity/ClassP/TimeConstructible.lean',
    'Encoding': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Encoding.lean',
    'Simulation': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Simulation.lean',
    'Catalog': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Catalog.lean',
    'H2Draft': 'audits/evidence/h2/StepBlockDraft.lean.txt',
}
IDENT = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_'!?]*(?:\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_'!?]*)*")


def strip_comments(text):
    out, depth, j = [], 0, 0
    while j < len(text):
        if depth > 0:
            if text.startswith('/-', j):
                depth += 1; j += 2; continue
            if text.startswith('-/', j):
                depth -= 1; j += 2; continue
            j += 1; continue
        if text.startswith('/-', j):
            depth += 1; j += 2; continue
        if text.startswith('--', j):
            k = text.find('\n', j)
            j = len(text) if k < 0 else k
            continue
        out.append(text[j]); j += 1
    return ''.join(out)


def norm(text):
    t = ' '.join(strip_comments(text).split())
    t = re.sub(r'^private ', '', t)
    t = re.sub(r'^lemma ', 'theorem ', t)
    t = re.sub(r'^noncomputable ', 'noncomputable ', t)
    return t


def rename(text, mapping):
    def sub(m):
        return '.'.join(mapping.get(p, p) for p in m.group(0).split('.'))
    return IDENT.sub(sub, text)


def decl_text(path, name, cache):
    if path not in cache:
        ds, lines = scan(path)
        cache[path] = (ds, lines)
    ds, lines = cache[path]
    hit = [d for d in ds if d['name'] == name]
    if len(hit) != 1:
        raise KeyError(f'{name}: {len(hit)} declarations in {os.path.basename(path)}')
    d = hit[0]
    return '\n'.join(lines[d['line'] - 1:d['end']]), d['line']


def split_stmt(t):
    """(statement, body) at the `:=` that opens the proof (whitespace-collapsed text)."""
    depth = 0
    cands = []
    for i, ch in enumerate(t):
        if ch in '([{⟨':
            depth += 1
        elif ch in ')]}⟩':
            depth -= 1
        elif depth == 0 and t.startswith(':=', i):
            cands.append(i)
    for i in cands:
        if t.startswith(':= by', i):
            return t[:i].strip(), t[i:].strip()
    i = cands[0]
    return t[:i].strip(), t[i:].strip()


def first_colon(stmt):
    """The statement colon: the first top-level `:` after the binders."""
    depth = 0
    for i, ch in enumerate(stmt):
        if ch in '([{⟨':
            depth += 1
        elif ch in ')]}⟩':
            depth -= 1
        elif depth == 0 and ch == ':' and not stmt.startswith(':=', i):
            return i
    return len(stmt)


def main():
    wt, unit, manifest = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
    units = [unit] + sys.argv[4:]
    renames = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, 'renames.json'), encoding='utf-8'))
    entries = json.load(open(manifest, encoding='utf-8'))
    cache = {}
    fails = 0
    counts = {}
    for e in entries:
        kind = e['kind']
        counts[kind] = counts.get(kind, 0) + 1
        try:
            g = None
            for u in units:
                try:
                    g, gline = decl_text(u, e['gate'], cache)
                    gfile = os.path.basename(u)
                    break
                except KeyError:
                    continue
            if g is None:
                raise KeyError(f"{e['gate']}: not found once in the unit files")
            src_path = os.path.join(wt, FILES[e['file']])
            s, sline = decl_text(src_path, e['source'], cache)
            mapping = renames.get(e.get('rename', ''), {})
            s = rename(s, mapping)
            gn, sn = norm(g), norm(s)
            for a, b in e.get('subst', []):
                if a not in sn:
                    raise ValueError(f'substitution source not found: {a!r}')
                sn = sn.replace(a, b)
            ok, why = True, ''
            if kind == 'verbatim':
                ok = gn == sn
                why = '' if ok else 'declarations differ'
            elif kind in ('statement', 'transform'):
                gs, gb = split_stmt(gn)
                ss, _ = split_stmt(sn)
                ok = gs == ss and gb in (':= by sorry', ':= sorry')
                why = '' if ok else ('statements differ' if gs != ss else f'gate body {gb!r}')
            elif kind == 'binders':
                gs, _ = split_stmt(gn)
                ss, _ = split_stmt(sn)
                gb, sb = gs[:first_colon(gs)].strip(), ss[:first_colon(ss)].strip()
                extra = e.get('gate_extra', '')
                # compare without the declaration names
                gb2 = gb.split(' ', 2)[2] if gb.count(' ') >= 2 else gb
                sb2 = sb.split(' ', 2)[2] if sb.count(' ') >= 2 else sb
                ok = gb2 == (sb2 + (' ' + extra if extra else '')).strip()
                why = '' if ok else 'binders differ'
            elif kind == 'substrings':
                body = strip_comments(g).split('\n')
                allow = [' '.join(a.split()) for a in e.get('allow', [])]
                flat = ' '.join(strip_comments(s).split())
                miss = []
                for l in body[1:]:
                    ln = ' '.join(l.split())
                    if ln and ln not in flat and ln not in allow:
                        miss.append(ln)
                ok = not miss
                why = '' if ok else 'not in source: ' + ' | '.join(miss)
            else:
                ok, why = False, f'unknown kind {kind}'
        except (KeyError, ValueError) as ex:
            ok, why = False, str(ex)
            gfile = gline = sline = '?'
        if not ok:
            fails += 1
            if os.environ.get('IDENTITY_DEBUG') and kind in ('verbatim', 'statement', 'transform'):
                print('   gate  :', gn[:2000])
                print('   source:', sn[:2000])
        print(f"{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'} {kind:10s} {e['gate']} ({gfile}:{gline}) <- "
              f"{e['file']}:{sline} {e['source']}"
              f"{' [rename ' + e['rename'] + ']' if e.get('rename') else ''}"
              f"{' [' + str(len(e.get('subst', []))) + ' substitutions]' if e.get('subst') else ''}"
              f"{'  -- ' + why if why else ''}")
    print(f"entries: {len(entries)}; by kind: {counts}; failures: {fails}")
    sys.exit(fails)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/scripts/gatenames.py =====

```
"""Full names of the declarations of a Lean file (namespace-aware). Read-only.
Usage: python3 -I gatenames.py <file.lean> [--public]
Prints `line kind visibility fullname` for every declaration; with --public only non-private
ones. Tracks `namespace`/`end` lines and `_root_.` prefixes; `example`s are skipped."""
import os
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from decls import scan  # noqa: E402
from region import strip_comments  # noqa: E402


def names(path):
    ds, lines = scan(path)
    lines = strip_comments(lines)
    starts = {d['line']: d for d in ds}
    stack, out = [], []
    for i, l in enumerate(lines, 1):
        if l.startswith('namespace '):
            stack.append(l.split()[1])
        elif l.startswith('end ') and stack and l.split()[1] == stack[-1]:
            stack.pop()
        if i in starts:
            d = starts[i]
            n = d['name']
            if not n:
                continue
            full = n[len('_root_.'):] if n.startswith('_root_.') else '.'.join(stack + [n])
            out.append((i, d['kind'], 'private' if d['private'] else 'public', full))
    return out


if __name__ == '__main__':
    pub = '--public' in sys.argv
    for i, k, v, f in names(sys.argv[1]):
        if pub and v == 'private':
            continue
        print(i, k, v, f)
```

## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/scripts/namescreen.py =====

```
"""MIG-1 name screen. Read-only; standard library only.

Usage: python3 -I namescreen.py <worktree> <gate-public.txt> <moved-names.json> <out.txt>

1. A namespace-aware index of every declaration of every `TCSlib` module (comment-stripped;
   `namespace`/`section`/`end` tracked; `_root_.` honoured; public and private).
2. For every proposed public name of the gate (the unit's public declarations, `MIG1Gate.*`
   excluded) with its home module: an exact full-name clash is any declaration with the same
   full name in the home module (other than the private declaration that the in-place rename
   makes public), in the home's import closure, or in any module that imports the home
   (Lean rejects a later private declaration whose name is already public). The H2 draft's
   proposed names (`audits/evidence/h2/StepBlockDraft.lean.txt`) are screened as a further
   module, since H2-M and MIG-1 land in the same window.
3. Short-name exposure: occurrences, as an identifier (bare or `FinTM.`-qualified), of every
   proposed short name in the colleague-owned files that open `Turing.FinTM` or sit in it
   (`TimeHierarchy/Separation.lean`, `CircuitComplexity/*`), and in every Catalog importer that
   does not import Primitives (it newly sees Primitives and TimeConstructible).
4. The same exact-clash test for the proposed private names of moved declarations
   (moved-names.json: {new name: home module}), against the home and its closure.
Mathlib and the other packages are screened by text: a proposed full name is reported if its
last component occurs in a package source file inside a `namespace Turing` block.
"""
import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys

KW = r'(theorem|lemma|def|abbrev|structure|inductive|instance|class|opaque|axiom)'
DPAT = re.compile(r'^(?:@\[[^\]]*\]\s*)?((?:private|protected|noncomputable|nonrec|partial|unsafe)\s+)*'
                  + KW + r'\s+([^\s:({\[]+)')


def strip(src):
    out, i, depth, n = [], 0, 0, len(src)
    while i < n:
        if src.startswith('/-', i):
            depth += 1; i += 2; continue
        if depth and src.startswith('-/', i):
            depth -= 1; i += 2; continue
        if depth:
            out.append('\n' if src[i] == '\n' else ' '); i += 1; continue
        if src.startswith('--', i):
            j = src.find('\n', i); j = n if j < 0 else j
            out.append(' ' * (j - i)); i = j; continue
        out.append(src[i]); i += 1
    return ''.join(out)


def index_file(path, mod):
    res = []
    stack = []
    for ln, l in enumerate(strip(open(path, encoding='utf-8').read()).split('\n'), 1):
        m = re.match(r'^namespace\s+(\S+)', l)
        if m:
            stack.append(('ns', m.group(1))); continue
        m = re.match(r'^(?:noncomputable\s+)?section\b\s*(\S*)', l)
        if m:
            stack.append(('sec', m.group(1))); continue
        m = re.match(r'^end\b\s*(\S*)', l)
        if m:
            if stack:
                stack.pop()
            continue
        m = DPAT.match(l)
        if m:
            name = m.group(3)
            if m.group(2) == 'instance' and (name.startswith('[') or name.startswith(':')):
                continue
            ns = '.'.join(n for k, n in stack if k == 'ns')
            full = name[len('_root_.'):] if name.startswith('_root_.') else (
                ns + '.' + name if ns else name)
            res.append(dict(mod=mod, line=ln, full=full, short=full.split('.')[-1],
                            private='private' in (m.group(1) or ''), kind=m.group(2)))
    return res


def main():
    wt, gate_list, moved_json, out = sys.argv[1:5]
    sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    from importgraph import graph, clos
    G = graph(wt)
    idx = []
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(wt, 'TCSlib', '**', '*.lean'), recursive=True)):
        mod = os.path.relpath(f, wt)[:-5].replace(os.sep, '.')
        idx.extend(index_file(f, mod))
    h2 = index_file(os.path.join(wt, 'audits/evidence/h2/StepBlockDraft.lean.txt'), 'H2-draft')
    for d in h2:
        if d['full'].startswith('Turing.Draft.StepBlock.'):
            short = d['full'][len('Turing.Draft.StepBlock.'):]
            generic = {'abs_workTapePos_runFrom_sub_le', 'inputPos_runFrom_of_inputTape_eq_zero',
                       'visitedByTapeHead_add_subset', 'visitedByTapeHead_step_subset'}
            keep = {'workReadsK', 'tableBitsK'}
            if short in generic:
                d['full'] = 'Turing.MultiTapeTM.' + short
            elif short in keep:
                d['full'] = 'Turing.' + short
            else:
                d['full'] = 'Turing.StepBlock.' + short
    lines = []
    w = lines.append
    w(f'index: {len(idx)} declarations in {len(set(d["mod"] for d in idx))} TCSlib modules; '
      f'H2 draft: {len(h2)} declarations')
    homes = {
        'Simulation': 'TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Simulation',
        'Composition': 'TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Composition',
        'Wrappers': 'TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Wrappers',
        'Encoding': 'TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Encoding',
        'TimeConstructible': 'TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.TimeConstructible',
        'Loop': 'TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Loop',
        'Primitives': 'TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Primitives',
        'Catalog': 'TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Catalog',
    }
    # gate-public.txt: "line kind visibility fullname"; homes by unit line ranges
    part_starts = json.load(open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(gate_list), 'part-lines.json')))
    prop = []
    for l in open(gate_list, encoding='utf-8'):
        ln, kind, vis, full = l.split()
        if '.MIG1Gate.' in full:
            continue
        ln = int(ln)
        home = max((s, h) for h, s in part_starts.items() if s <= ln)[1]
        prop.append((full, homes[home]))
    # in-place renames: the private source that becomes the public name
    renamed = json.load(open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                                          'inplace.json')))
    mods = [m for m in G if m != 'TCSlib']
    imp_by = {m: set(x for x in mods if m in clos(G, x)) for m in homes.values()}
    clash_total = 0
    w('')
    w('## 1. Exact full-name clashes of the proposed public names')
    for full, home in prop:
        scope = {home} | clos(G, home) | imp_by[home]
        hits = []
        for d in idx:
            if d['full'] != full or d['mod'] not in scope:
                continue
            src = renamed.get(full)
            if src and d['mod'] == home and d['private'] and src == d['full']:
                continue
            hits.append(d)
        for d in h2:
            if d['full'] == full and full != 'Turing.MultiTapeTM.abs_workTapePos_runFrom_sub_le':
                hits.append(d)
        if hits:
            clash_total += len(hits)
            w(f'CLASH {full} (home {home.split(".")[-1]}): ' + '; '.join(
                f"{d['mod']}:{d['line']} {'private' if d['private'] else 'public'} {d['kind']}"
                for d in hits))
    w(f'proposed public names: {len(prop)}; clashes: {clash_total}')
    w('in-place renames (the private source made public, not a clash): ' +
      ', '.join(f'{k} <- private {v}' for k, v in renamed.items()))
    w('shared with H2 by design: Turing.MultiTapeTM.abs_workTapePos_runFrom_sub_le')
    # 2. same short names elsewhere (information)
    w('')
    w('## 2. The same last component elsewhere in TCSlib (information; other namespaces)')
    shorts = {}
    for full, home in prop:
        shorts.setdefault(full.split('.')[-1], []).append(full)
    for s, fulls in sorted(shorts.items()):
        others = sorted({d['full'] for d in idx if d['short'] == s and d['full'] not in fulls
                         and d['full'] not in renamed.values()})
        if others:
            w(f'{s}: ' + ', '.join(others[:8]) + (' …' if len(others) > 8 else ''))
    # 3. exposure in colleague files and the eight new Catalog importers
    w('')
    w('## 3. Identifier occurrences of the proposed short names (bare or `FinTM.`-qualified)')
    files = [os.path.join(wt, 'TCSlib/Complexity/TimeHierarchy/Separation.lean')] + sorted(
        glob.glob(os.path.join(wt, 'TCSlib/Complexity/CircuitComplexity/**/*.lean'), recursive=True))
    newimp = sorted(m for m in imp_by[homes['Catalog']] if homes['Primitives'] not in clos(G, m))
    w('Catalog importers that newly see Primitives and TimeConstructible: ' +
      ', '.join(m.split('.')[-1] for m in newimp))
    for m in newimp:
        files.append(os.path.join(wt, *m.split('.')) + '.lean')
    occ = 0
    for f in files:
        s = strip(open(f, encoding='utf-8').read())
        for short in sorted(shorts):
            for pref in ['', 'FinTM.']:
                pat = re.compile(r'(?<![\w.\'])' + re.escape(pref + short) + r'(?![\w\'])')
                n = len(pat.findall(s))
                if n:
                    occ += n
                    w(f'{os.path.relpath(f, wt)}: {pref + short} x{n}')
    w(f'files screened: {len(files)}; occurrences: {occ}')
    # 4. moved private names
    w('')
    w('## 4. Proposed private names of moved declarations')
    moved = json.load(open(moved_json, encoding='utf-8'))
    mclash = 0
    for name, home in moved.items():
        scope = {homes[home]} | clos(G, homes[home]) | imp_by[homes[home]]
        hits = [d for d in idx if d['full'] == name and d['mod'] in scope
                and (not d['private'] or d['mod'] == homes[home])]
        hits += [d for d in idx if d['full'] == name and d['private'] and d['mod'] in scope
                 and d['mod'] != homes[home] and d['mod'] != homes['Catalog']]
        if hits:
            mclash += len(hits)
            w(f'CLASH {name} (home {home}): ' + '; '.join(
                f"{d['mod']}:{d['line']} {'private' if d['private'] else 'public'}" for d in hits))
    w(f'moved names: {len(moved)}; clashes: {mclash}')
    # 5. package sources
    w('')
    w('## 5. Package sources (text): proposed last components inside `namespace Turing` blocks')
    pk = 0
    for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(wt, '.lake', 'packages', '*', '**', '*.lean'), recursive=True):
        txt = open(f, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
        if 'namespace Turing' not in txt:
            continue
        for short in shorts:
            if re.search(r'(?<![\w.])' + re.escape(short) + r'(?![\w\'])', txt):
                pk += 1
                w(f'{os.path.relpath(f, wt)}: {short}')
    w(f'package hits: {pk}')
    open(out, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write('\n'.join(lines) + '\n')
    print('\n'.join(lines[:3]))
    print(f'clashes {clash_total}, exposure occurrences {occ}, moved clashes {mclash}, '
          f'package hits {pk}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

"""Screen the MIG-1 proposed names against another tree of landing files (e.g. MIG-0b's round-2
landing set). Read-only. Usage: python3 -I namescreen_extra.py <landing root> <gate-public.txt>
<moved-names.json>. Reports exact full-name matches and shared last components."""

## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/scripts/consumers.py =====

```
"""Code citations of named declarations across all TCSlib modules. Read-only.

Usage: python3 -I consumers.py <worktree> <names.json> <out.json>

names.json: list of [home module, short name]. For each name: every identifier occurrence
(bare or qualified, last component equal to the name, not followed by an identifier character)
in the comment-stripped code of every `TCSlib` module, minus the declaration's own header
line; reported per file with line numbers, split into the home file (internal) and the others
(external). The script also checks that each name is declared exactly once in the tree, so
that the textual matches are unambiguous. Docstring and comment mentions are counted
separately ("doc").
"""
import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from namescreen import strip, index_file  # noqa: E402


def main():
    wt, names_json, out = sys.argv[1:4]
    names = json.load(open(names_json, encoding='utf-8'))
    files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(wt, 'TCSlib', '**', '*.lean'), recursive=True))
    src = {}
    code = {}
    idx = []
    for f in files:
        mod = os.path.relpath(f, wt)[:-5].replace(os.sep, '.')
        s = open(f, encoding='utf-8').read()
        src[mod] = s.split('\n')
        code[mod] = strip(s).split('\n')
        idx.extend(index_file(f, mod))
    res = {}
    for home, name in names:
        decl = [d for d in idx if d['short'] == name]
        pat = re.compile(r'(?<![\w\'])(?:[\w\']+\.)*' + re.escape(name) + r'(?![\w\'])')
        ext, internal, doc = [], [], []
        for mod in code:
            for i, l in enumerate(code[mod], 1):
                if any(d['mod'] == mod and d['line'] == i for d in decl):
                    continue
                n = len(pat.findall(l))
                if n:
                    (internal if mod == home else ext).append([mod, i, n])
                raw = src[mod][i - 1]
                nd = len(pat.findall(raw)) - n
                if nd > 0:
                    doc.append([mod, i, nd])
        res[name] = dict(home=home, declared=[[d['mod'], d['line'], d['private']] for d in decl],
                         internal=internal, external=ext, doc=doc)
    json.dump(res, open(out, 'w', encoding='utf-8'), indent=1)
    tot = sum(sum(n for _, _, n in r['external']) for r in res.values())
    files_ext = {m for r in res.values() for m, _, _ in r['external']}
    for name, r in res.items():
        e = sum(n for _, _, n in r['external'])
        fs = sorted({m.split('.')[-1] for m, _, _ in r['external']})
        print(f"{name}: declared {len(r['declared'])}; internal "
              f"{sum(n for _, _, n in r['internal'])}; external {e} in {len(fs)} files"
              f"{': ' + ', '.join(fs) if fs else ''}; doc {sum(n for _, _, n in r['doc'])}")
    print(f'total external citations: {tot} in {len(files_ext)} files')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/scripts/importgraph.py =====

```
"""Import graph of a TCSlib worktree, from the `import` lines of every module. Read-only.
Usage: python3 -I importgraph.py <worktree> closure <Module> ...   (transitive TCSlib imports)
       python3 -I importgraph.py <worktree> replay <Module> ...    (modules equal to or importing any)
       python3 -I importgraph.py <worktree> importers <Module>     (direct and transitive importers)
"""
import sys, glob, os


def graph(root):
    G = {}
    for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, 'TCSlib', '**', '*.lean'), recursive=True):
        m = os.path.relpath(f, root)[:-5].replace(os.sep, '.')
        G[m] = [l.split()[1] for l in open(f, encoding='utf-8') if l.startswith('import ')]
    top = os.path.join(root, 'TCSlib.lean')
    if os.path.isfile(top):
        G['TCSlib'] = [l.split()[1] for l in open(top, encoding='utf-8') if l.startswith('import ')]
    return G


def clos(G, m):
    seen, st = set(), [m]
    while st:
        x = st.pop()
        for y in G.get(x, []):
            if y.startswith('TCSlib') and y not in seen:
                seen.add(y); st.append(y)
    return seen


if __name__ == '__main__':
    root, mode, mods = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3:]
    G = graph(root)
    mods_in = [m for m in G if m != 'TCSlib']
    if mode == 'closure':
        for m in mods:
            print(m, '->', ' '.join(sorted(clos(G, m))))
    elif mode == 'replay':
        S = set(mods)
        R = sorted(m for m in mods_in if m in S or clos(G, m) & S)
        print(f'modules: {len(mods_in)}; replay closure: {len(R)}')
        from collections import Counter
        c = Counter('.'.join(m.split('.')[:3]) for m in R)
        for k, v in sorted(c.items()):
            print(f'  {k}: {v}')
        for m in R:
            print('  ', m)
    elif mode == 'importers':
        for m in mods:
            d = sorted(x for x in mods_in if m in G[x])
            t = sorted(x for x in mods_in if m in clos(G, x))
            print(m, 'direct', len(d), 'transitive', len(t))
            for x in d:
                print('  direct', x)
```

## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/scripts/region.py =====

```
"""MIG-1 deletion plan: classify every declaration of the `Build/Catalog.lean` region.

Usage: python3 -I region.py <worktree> <outdir>

Read-only on the worktree; standard library only. Writes <outdir>/deletion-plan.json and
<outdir>/deletion-plan.tsv and prints the counts.

Method.
* Declarations: `decls.scan` (comment-aware scanner) of Catalog; the region is the
  `namespace Turing.FinTM` block between the first `f2_` docstring and its `end`.
* Code of a declaration: its lines from the keyword to the line before the next top-level
  command, comments and docstrings removed, trailing blanks dropped, each line right-stripped.
  "With docstrings" line counts add the immediately preceding docstring block.
* A copy's source: the declaration of the same name, after removing the prefix (`f2_`, or
  `catalog_redirect` -> `redirect`), in one of the seven home files.
* Code-identical: the copy's code with every region-local prefixed identifier renamed to its
  unprefixed form equals the source's code. Statement-identical: the same on the statement
  (the code up to the first top-level `:=` or `where`).
* Dependencies: identifier occurrences in code; closures run over region declarations.
* Fates follow the MIG-1 statement-gate plan (the pack, section "Deletion plan"): see FATE below.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from decls import scan  # noqa: E402

HOMES = {
    'Composition': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Composition.lean',
    'Primitives': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Primitives.lean',
    'Loop': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Loop.lean',
    'Wrappers': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Wrappers.lean',
    'TimeConstructible': 'TCSlib/Complexity/ClassP/TimeConstructible.lean',
    'Encoding': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Encoding.lean',
    'Simulation': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Simulation.lean',
}
CATALOG = 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Catalog.lean'
IDENT = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_'!?]*(?:\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_'!?]*)*")


def strip_comments(lines):
    out, depth = [], 0
    for s in lines:
        o, j = '', 0
        while j < len(s):
            if depth > 0:
                if s.startswith('/-', j):
                    depth += 1; j += 2; continue
                if s.startswith('-/', j):
                    depth -= 1; j += 2; continue
                j += 1; continue
            if s.startswith('/-', j):
                depth += 1; j += 2; continue
            if s.startswith('--', j):
                break
            o += s[j]; j += 1
        out.append(o.rstrip())
    return out


def doc_start(lines, line):
    s = line - 1
    j = s - 1
    while j >= 0 and lines[j].startswith('@['):
        j -= 1
    if j >= 0 and lines[j].rstrip().endswith('-/'):
        k = j
        while k >= 0 and not lines[k].lstrip().startswith('/--') and not lines[k].lstrip().startswith('/-'):
            k -= 1
        if k >= 0 and lines[k].lstrip().startswith('/--'):
            return k + 1
    return line


def code_of(code, d):
    c = code[d['line'] - 1:d['end']]
    while c and c[-1] == '':
        c.pop()
    return [l for l in c]


def statement(c):
    """Code up to the first top-level `:=` / ` where` (joined, whitespace-normalized)."""
    text = '\n'.join(c)
    depth = 0
    for i, ch in enumerate(text):
        if ch in '([{⟨':
            depth += 1
        elif ch in ')]}⟩':
            depth -= 1
        elif depth == 0 and text.startswith(':=', i):
            return ' '.join(text[:i].split())
        elif depth == 0 and text.startswith(' where', i) and (i + 6 == len(text) or text[i + 6] in ' \n'):
            return ' '.join(text[:i].split())
    return ' '.join(text.split())


def unprefix(name):
    if name.startswith('f2_'):
        return name[3:]
    if name.startswith('catalog_redirect'):
        return 'redirect' + name[len('catalog_redirect'):]
    return None


def rename(lines, mapping):
    def sub(m):
        tok = m.group(0)
        parts = tok.split('.')
        return '.'.join(mapping.get(p, p) for p in parts)
    return [IDENT.sub(sub, l) for l in lines]


def main():
    wt, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    cat_lines = open(os.path.join(wt, CATALOG), encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
    cat_code = strip_comments(cat_lines)
    D, _ = scan(os.path.join(wt, CATALOG))
    first = min(d['line'] for d in D if d['name'].startswith('f2_'))
    start = max(i + 1 for i, l in enumerate(cat_lines[:first]) if l.startswith('namespace Turing.FinTM'))
    end = min(i + 1 for i, l in enumerate(cat_lines) if i + 1 > first and l.startswith('end Turing.FinTM'))
    region = [d for d in D if start < d['line'] < end]
    homes = {}
    for k, rel in HOMES.items():
        hl = open(os.path.join(wt, rel), encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
        hd, _ = scan(os.path.join(wt, rel))
        homes[k] = (hl, strip_comments(hl), hd)
    index = {}
    for k in HOMES:
        for d in homes[k][2]:
            index.setdefault(d['name'], (k, d))
    names = {d['name'] for d in region}
    rmap = {n: unprefix(n) for n in names if unprefix(n)}
    rows = []
    code = {}
    for d in region:
        c = code_of(cat_code, d)
        code[d['name']] = c
        ds = doc_start(cat_lines, d['line'])
        r = dict(name=d['name'], line=d['line'], end=d['end'], kind=d['kind'],
                 private=d['private'], lines=d['end'] - d['line'] + 1,
                 lines_doc=d['end'] - ds + 1)
        base = unprefix(d['name'])
        if d['name'].startswith('f2_'):
            r['family'] = 'f2'
        elif d['name'].startswith('a2_'):
            r['family'] = 'a2'
        elif d['name'].startswith('catalog_redirect'):
            r['family'] = 'catalog_redirect'
        elif not d['private']:
            r['family'] = 'public'
        else:
            r['family'] = 'other-private'
        r['source'] = None
        if base and base in index:
            k, sd = index[base]
            hc = code_of(homes[k][1], sd)
            mine = rename(c, rmap)
            r['source'] = f"{k}:{sd['line']}:{base}"
            r['code_identical'] = [l.strip() for l in mine if l.strip()] == [l.strip() for l in hc if l.strip()]
            r['statement_identical'] = statement(mine) == statement(hc)
        rows.append(r)
    # dependencies inside the region
    uses = {}
    for r in rows:
        toks = set()
        for l in code[r['name']]:
            for t in IDENT.findall(l):
                toks.update(t.split('.'))
        uses[r['name']] = sorted(t for t in toks if t in names and t != r['name'])
    # instances are used implicitly: attach each instance to the inductive it is about
    for r in rows:
        if r['kind'] == 'instance':
            for t in uses[r['name']]:
                if t in names:
                    uses.setdefault(t, [])
                    if r['name'] not in uses[t]:
                        uses[t] = sorted(uses[t] + [r['name']])
    for r in rows:
        r['uses'] = uses[r['name']]
    by = {r['name']: r for r in rows}

    def leaf(n):
        r = by[n]
        return r['source'] is not None  # a copy: the home original is used instead

    def closure(roots, through_copies=False):
        seen, todo = set(), list(roots)
        while todo:
            n = todo.pop()
            if n in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(n)
            if leaf(n) and n not in roots and not through_copies:
                continue
            todo.extend(uses[n])
        return seen

    plan = json.load(open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), 'fates.json'),
                          encoding='utf-8'))
    families = plan['moved_families']
    absorbed = plan['absorbed']
    duplicates = plan['duplicates']
    replaces = plan['replaces']
    publics = plan['publics']
    reach = {}
    for fam, spec in families.items():
        for n in closure(spec['roots']):
            reach.setdefault(n, []).append(fam)
    # reach from every public row through everything (to find dead declarations)
    pub_names = [r['name'] for r in rows if r['family'] == 'public']
    live_all = closure(pub_names, through_copies=True)
    sform = set(closure(plan['sform_roots'], through_copies=True))
    others = set()
    for p in pub_names:
        if p in plan['sform_roots']:
            continue
        others |= closure([p], through_copies=True)
    for r in rows:
        n = r['name']
        fams = reach.get(n, [])
        if r['family'] == 'public':
            r['fate'] = publics[n]['fate']
            r['detail'] = publics[n]['detail']
        elif n in absorbed:
            r['fate'] = 'absorbed into a gated public statement'
            r['detail'] = absorbed[n]
        elif n in replaces:
            r['fate'] = 'move: replaces the original (extended statement)'
            r['detail'] = replaces[n]
        elif n in duplicates:
            r['fate'] = 'delete: duplicates an existing public declaration'
            r['detail'] = duplicates[n]
        elif r['source'] is not None and r.get('code_identical'):
            r['fate'] = 'delete: copy, original used'
            r['detail'] = r['source']
        elif r['source'] is not None and r.get('statement_identical'):
            r['fate'] = 'delete: statement-identical copy (proof differs), original used'
            r['detail'] = r['source']
        elif r['source'] is not None:
            r['fate'] = 'delete: modified copy, citations re-targeted at the original'
            r['detail'] = r['source']
        elif fams:
            fam = fams[0]
            r['fate'] = 'move'
            r['detail'] = f"{families[fam]['home']} ({fam})"
        elif n not in live_all:
            r['fate'] = 'delete: dead (reached from no public declaration)'
            r['detail'] = ''
        elif n in sform and n not in others:
            r['fate'] = 'delete: reached only from the decision-loop S-form proof (dropped)'
            r['detail'] = ''
        else:
            r['fate'] = 'UNASSIGNED'
            r['detail'] = ''
        r['families'] = fams
    # declarations whose every user is deleted (and that no kept family reaches)
    users = {r['name']: [q['name'] for q in rows if r['name'] in q['uses']] for r in rows}
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for r in rows:
            if r['fate'] != 'UNASSIGNED':
                continue
            us = users[r['name']]
            if us and all(by[u]['fate'].startswith('delete') for u in us):
                r['fate'] = 'delete: used only by deleted declarations'
                r['detail'] = ', '.join(us)
                changed = True
    # proposed private names of the moved declarations (prefix dropped, `a2_map` -> `fwdMap`)
    ns_of = {'ClassP/TimeConstructible.lean': 'Complexity.'}
    special = plan.get('new_names', {})
    moved = {}
    for r in rows:
        if not r['fate'].startswith('move') or r['family'] == 'public':
            continue
        n = r['name']
        if n in special:
            new = special[n]
        elif n.startswith('a2_map'):
            new = 'fwdMap' + n[len('a2_map'):]
        elif n.startswith('a2_Map'):
            new = 'FwdMap' + n[len('a2_Map'):]
        else:
            new = n[3:] if n.startswith('f2_') else n
        home = families[r['families'][0]]['home'] if r['families'] else 'Build/Loop.lean'
        full = ns_of.get(home, 'Turing.FinTM.') + new
        r['new_name'] = full
        moved[full] = home.split('/')[-1][:-5]
    json.dump(moved, open(os.path.join(out, 'moved-names.json'), 'w'), indent=1)
    json.dump(dict(region=[start, end], rows=rows), open(os.path.join(out, 'deletion-plan.json'), 'w'),
              indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
    with open(os.path.join(out, 'deletion-plan.tsv'), 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write('line\tend\tname\tkind\tfamily\tlines\tlines_doc\tsource\tcode_identical\t'
                'statement_identical\tfate\tdetail\tnew_name\n')
        for r in rows:
            f.write('\t'.join(str(x) for x in [r['line'], r['end'], r['name'], r['kind'], r['family'],
                                              r['lines'], r['lines_doc'], r['source'] or '',
                                              r.get('code_identical', ''),
                                              r.get('statement_identical', ''), r['fate'],
                                              r['detail'], r.get('new_name', '')]) + '\n')
    # summary
    from collections import Counter, defaultdict
    print(f'region: lines {start}-{end} ({end - start + 1} lines); declarations {len(rows)}')
    c = Counter(r['family'] for r in rows)
    print('families:', dict(c))
    f2 = [r for r in rows if r['family'] == 'f2']
    print('f2 with same-named source:', sum(1 for r in f2 if r['source']),
          '; code-identical:', sum(1 for r in f2 if r.get('code_identical')),
          '(lines with docstrings', sum(r['lines_doc'] for r in f2 if r.get('code_identical')), ')',
          '; statement-identical only:', sum(1 for r in f2 if r['source'] and not r.get('code_identical')
                                              and r.get('statement_identical')),
          '; differing:', sum(1 for r in f2 if r['source'] and not r.get('statement_identical')),
          '; no source:', sum(1 for r in f2 if not r['source']))
    cr = [r for r in rows if r['family'] == 'catalog_redirect']
    print('catalog_redirect code-identical:', sum(1 for r in cr if r.get('code_identical')), 'of', len(cr))
    fc = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0])
    for r in rows:
        k = r['fate'] if r['fate'] != 'move' else 'move: ' + r['detail']
        fc[(r['family'], k)][0] += 1
        fc[(r['family'], k)][1] += r['lines_doc']
    for (fam, k), (n, l) in sorted(fc.items()):
        print(f'  {fam:17s} {k}: {n} decls, {l} lines with docstrings')
    print('UNASSIGNED:', [r['name'] for r in rows if r['fate'] == 'UNASSIGNED'])


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/scripts/runall.sh =====

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# MIG-1 statement gate: rebuild every artifact and rerun every check (read-only on the worktree).
# Usage: [MIG0B_LANDING=<dir>] bash runall.sh <worktree> <olean snapshot> <leanelab.sh> <gate dir>
# Writes <gate dir>/logs/mig1-statements-{elaboration,identity,axioms,cutcheck,names,
# consumers,replay}.log. Elaboration goes only through leanelab.sh (no olean output).
set -u
WT="$1"; OL="$2"; ELAB="$3"; G="$4"
cd "$G" || exit 1
P="python3 -I"
mkdir -p logs cuts data work probes lintdir
LOG=logs/mig1-statements-elaboration.log
: > "$LOG"
say() { printf '%s\n' "$*" | tee -a "$LOG"; }
elab() {  # elab <label> <file>
  local out="work/$(basename "$2").out"
  bash "$ELAB" "$WT" "$OL" "$G/$2" > "$out" 2>&1
  local e=$?
  say "$1: $2 -- exit $e; errors $(grep -c ': error' "$out"); 'declaration uses sorry' warnings $(grep -c "declaration uses 'sorry'" "$out"); other warnings $(grep ': warning' "$out" | grep -vc "declaration uses 'sorry'"); lines $(wc -l < "$2" | tr -d ' ')"
}
say "# MIG-1 statement gate, elaboration log"
say "worktree HEAD: $(cat "$(sed -n 's/^gitdir: //p' "$WT/.git")/HEAD" 2>/dev/null) (read from the git metadata file; no git command)"
say "olean snapshot: $OL; toolchain file: $(cat "$WT/lean-toolchain")"
say ""
say "## 1. Build of the unit and the probes from their templates (scripts/build_unit.py)"
$P scripts/build_unit.py "$WT" parts MIG1Statements.lean && say "built MIG1Statements.lean"
$P scripts/build_unit.py "$WT" probe-parts work/probe-tail.lean && cat MIG1Statements.lean work/probe-tail.lean > probes/SpecProbe.lean && say "built probes/SpecProbe.lean (the unit followed by the spec-probe tail)"
$P scripts/build_unit.py "$WT" bridge-parts probes/BridgeProbe.lean && say "built probes/BridgeProbe.lean"
say ""
say "## 2. Elaboration"
elab "unit" MIG1Statements.lean
elab "spec probe" probes/SpecProbe.lean
elab "bridge probe" probes/BridgeProbe.lean
say ""
say "## 3. Cut checks (scripts/cutcheck.py, from audits/evidence/stage2-gate/scripts/)"
rm -f cuts/*.check.lean
$P scripts/cutcheck.py MIG1Statements.lean "$WT" cuts > logs/mig1-statements-cutcheck.log
cat logs/mig1-statements-cutcheck.log >> "$LOG"
for f in cuts/*.check.lean; do elab "cut" "$f"; done
grep "^cut" "$LOG" >> logs/mig1-statements-cutcheck.log
say ""
say "## 4. Identity (scripts/identity.py) and its negative controls"
$P scripts/identity.py "$WT" MIG1Statements.lean scripts/identity-manifest.json work/probe-tail.lean probes/BridgeProbe.lean > logs/mig1-statements-identity.log
say "identity: exit $? ($(tail -1 logs/mig1-statements-identity.log))"
$P - <<'EOF'
s = open('MIG1Statements.lean').read()
for a, b in [("            controlAction .neg (some (.inr (.inr (.inl (b, true)))))",
              "            controlAction .pos (some (.inr (.inr (.inl (b, true)))))"),
             ("(prependTM w).ComputesFunInTime (fun x => w ++ x) (fun n => w.length + n + 1) := by",
              "(prependTM w).ComputesFunInTime (fun x => w ++ x) (fun n => w.length + n + 2) := by"),
             ("          | some _ => act 0 none (none, .neg) (none, .neg) none (some (ctrl 3))",
              "          | some _ => act 0 none (none, .neg) (none, .pos) none (some (ctrl 3))")]:
    assert s.count(a) == 1, a
    s = s.replace(a, b)
open('work/mutant.lean', 'w').write(s)
EOF
$P scripts/identity.py "$WT" work/mutant.lean scripts/identity-manifest.json work/probe-tail.lean probes/BridgeProbe.lean > work/identity-control.out
say "negative controls (three single-token mutations: a timedCondTM transition, the prependTM_computes bound, a loopHostM transition): $(grep -c '^FAIL' work/identity-control.out) failures, expected 3"
{ echo; echo "## negative controls"; grep '^FAIL' work/identity-control.out; } >> logs/mig1-statements-identity.log
say ""
say "## 5. Axioms (probes/AxiomProbe.lean: the unit followed by #print axioms of its public declarations)"
$P scripts/gatenames.py MIG1Statements.lean --public > work/gate-public.txt
{ cat MIG1Statements.lean; printf '\n/-! Axiom probe (not landed): every public declaration of the unit. -/\n\n'; awk '{print "#print axioms " $4}' work/gate-public.txt; } > probes/AxiomProbe.lean
bash "$ELAB" "$WT" "$OL" "$G/probes/AxiomProbe.lean" > work/axioms.out 2>&1
say "axiom probe: exit $?"
$P - <<'EOF' > logs/mig1-statements-axioms.log
import re
t = open('work/axioms.out').read()
items = re.findall(r"'([^']+)' (depends on axioms: \[([^\]]*)\]|does not depend on any axioms)", t, re.S)
std = {'propext', 'Classical.choice', 'Quot.sound'}
res = [(n, [a.strip() for a in ax.replace('\n', ' ').split(',') if a.strip()]) for n, _, ax in items]
print(f'declarations reported: {len(res)}')
print(f'non-standard axioms (other than propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, sorryAx): '
      f'{[n for n, a in res if set(a) - std - {"sorryAx"}]}')
print(f'with sorryAx: {sum(1 for _, a in res if "sorryAx" in a)}; '
      f'sorry-free: {sum(1 for _, a in res if "sorryAx" not in a)}')
print()
for n, a in res:
    print(f"{n}: {', '.join(a) if a else '(none)'}")
EOF
head -3 logs/mig1-statements-axioms.log >> "$LOG"
say ""
say "## 6. Names (scripts/namescreen.py)"
$P - <<'EOF'
import json
lines = open('MIG1Statements.lean').read().split('\n')
json.dump({l.split()[2].split('.')[-1]: i for i, l in enumerate(lines, 1)
           if l.startswith('-- @landing ')}, open('work/part-lines.json', 'w'))
EOF
$P scripts/namescreen.py "$WT" work/gate-public.txt data/moved-names.json logs/mig1-statements-names.log | tail -1 | tee -a "$LOG"
if [ -n "${MIG0B_LANDING:-}" ]; then  # optional: MIG-0b's round-2 landing set (not in the worktree)
  { echo; echo "## 6. The MIG-0b round-2 landing set ($MIG0B_LANDING)"; \
    $P scripts/namescreen_extra.py "$MIG0B_LANDING" work/gate-public.txt data/moved-names.json; } \
    >> logs/mig1-statements-names.log
  tail -3 logs/mig1-statements-names.log | tee -a "$LOG"
fi
say ""
say "## 7. Widths and style"
$P scripts/widths.py MIG1Statements.lean probes/SpecProbe.lean probes/BridgeProbe.lean | tail -1 | tee -a "$LOG"
rm -f lintdir/*.lean; cp MIG1Statements.lean probes/SpecProbe.lean probes/BridgeProbe.lean lintdir/
$P scripts/campaign_style_lint.py lintdir 2>&1 | tail -6 | tee -a "$LOG"
say ""
say "## 8. Consumers of the rows (scripts/consumers.py) and replay closure (scripts/importgraph.py)"
$P scripts/consumers.py "$WT" work/consumer-names.json data/consumers.json > logs/mig1-statements-consumers.log
tail -1 logs/mig1-statements-consumers.log | tee -a "$LOG"
T=TCSlib.Complexity
{
  for set in "whole MIG-1 (ten files):$T.TuringMachine.Simulation $T.TuringMachine.Composition $T.TuringMachine.Build.Wrappers $T.TuringMachine.Encoding $T.ClassP.TimeConstructible $T.TuringMachine.Build.Loop $T.TuringMachine.Build.Primitives $T.TuringMachine.Build.Catalog $T.TuringMachine.Build.CertShell $T.TuringMachine.CodeSimulator" \
             "PR S (statements):$T.TuringMachine.Simulation $T.TuringMachine.Composition $T.TuringMachine.Build.Wrappers $T.TuringMachine.Encoding $T.ClassP.TimeConstructible $T.TuringMachine.Build.Loop $T.TuringMachine.Build.Primitives $T.TuringMachine.Build.Catalog" \
             "F-A:$T.TuringMachine.Composition $T.TuringMachine.Simulation $T.TuringMachine.Build.Wrappers $T.TuringMachine.Encoding $T.ClassP.TimeConstructible" \
             "F-B:$T.TuringMachine.Build.Primitives" \
             "F-C:$T.TuringMachine.Build.Loop" \
             "F-D:$T.TuringMachine.Build.Catalog $T.TuringMachine.Build.CertShell $T.TuringMachine.CodeSimulator" \
             "F-D without CodeSimulator:$T.TuringMachine.Build.Catalog $T.TuringMachine.Build.CertShell"; do
    echo "== ${set%%:*}"

} > logs/mig1-statements-replay.log
grep -A1 "^==" logs/mig1-statements-replay.log | grep -v "^--" | paste - - | tee -a "$LOG"

## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/scripts/build_unit.py =====

```
"""Assemble the MIG-1 statement-gate unit from its part templates. Read-only on the worktree.

Usage: python3 -I build_unit.py <worktree> <parts-dir> <out.lean>

Each template line of the form
    -- @@verbatim <FileKey> <RenameKey|-> [--public] [--nodoc] [--stmt] <name> ...
is replaced by the verbatim text of the named declarations of that home file (scripts/mkshim.py),
with the rename map `RenameKey` of scripts/renames.json applied. Everything else is copied as is.
The templates (`*.lean`, or `*.lean.txt` as kept under `audits/`) are concatenated in file-name
order.
"""
import glob
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
FILES = {
    'Composition': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Composition.lean',
    'Primitives': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Primitives.lean',
    'Loop': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Loop.lean',
    'Wrappers': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Wrappers.lean',
    'TimeConstructible': 'TCSlib/Complexity/ClassP/TimeConstructible.lean',
    'Encoding': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Encoding.lean',
    'Simulation': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Simulation.lean',
    'Catalog': 'TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Catalog.lean',
    'H2Draft': 'audits/evidence/h2/StepBlockDraft.lean.txt',
}


def main():
    wt, parts, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
    renames = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, 'renames.json'), encoding='utf-8'))
    wraps = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, 'wraps.json'), encoding='utf-8'))
    chunks = []
    srcs = glob.glob(os.path.join(parts, '*.lean')) + glob.glob(os.path.join(parts, '*.lean.txt'))
    for p in sorted(srcs, key=os.path.basename):
        lines = open(p, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
        res = []
        for l in lines:
            if l.startswith('-- @@verbatim '):
                w = l.split()[2:]
                fkey, rkey, rest = w[0], w[1], w[2:]
                rpath = '-'
                if rkey != '-':
                    rpath = os.path.join(HERE, '.rename-' + rkey + '.json')
                    json.dump(renames[rkey], open(rpath, 'w', encoding='utf-8'))
                txt = subprocess.run(
                    [sys.executable, '-I', os.path.join(HERE, 'mkshim.py'),
                     os.path.join(wt, FILES[fkey]), rpath] + rest,
                    check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.rstrip('\n')
                if rpath != '-':
                    os.remove(rpath)
                # wrap verbatim lines over 100 characters by the recorded line breaks
                # (scripts/wraps.json: whole-line replacements inside argument parentheses;
                # the identity check compares modulo whitespace)
                txt = '\n'.join(wraps.get(l, l) for l in txt.split('\n'))
                res.append(txt)
            else:
                res.append(l)
        chunks.append('\n'.join(res).rstrip('\n') + '\n')
    with open(out, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write('\n'.join(chunks))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Simulation
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Composition
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Wrappers
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Encoding
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.TimeConstructible
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Loop
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Primitives
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Catalog

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# MIG-1 statement gate: named witnesses, their spec theorems, the rows as corollaries

**Status: the statement-gate unit of backlog row MIG-1; not a library file.** It elaborates
against the campaign snapshot, in which today's rows are public and today's witnesses private.
The unit has eight parts, one per home file, each opened by a section comment beginning `════`
and by `-- @landing` and `-- @imports` lines. Landing is a set of edits to the existing home
modules, not a new module:

* **Witness definitions.** A witness that is today a private definition of its home file
  (`idTM`, `constTM`, `ifEqTM`, `condTM`, `timedCondTM`, `Turing.pairDiagTM`, `lengthBitsTM`,
  `prependTM`, `incFixedTM`, `pairValidTM`, `pairExtractTM`, `unaryTokenTM`, `appendBitTM`,
  `loopHostTM`, `callTM`) lands by an asserted scripted rename **in place**: the `private`
  keyword goes, the name changes by the rename map of the pack, the body is unchanged, and the
  docstring becomes the one given here. Every other witness (`toCodeTM`, `polyUnaryTM`,
  `polyBitsTM`, `pairLenCheckTM`, `stripLastTM`, `pairMapSndTM`, `splitSolveTM`,
  `splitSolveWithTM`, `emitLoopTM`, `callEntry`, `callExit`) is a new definition whose body is
  today's witness term, from the row proof named in its docstring. `pairMapSndTM` alone lands
  at the fill stage, with the forwarding-controller family that moves from Catalog. The bodies
  here are the source bodies verbatim modulo the rename map
  (`audits/logs/mig1-statements-identity.log`).
* **Gate shims** (blocks between `-- @shim begin` and `-- @shim end`) are verbatim copies of
  private definitions that a witness body uses. They exist only because a private declaration
  cannot be named from another module; on landing they are dropped, since the originals are
  already in the home file (or, for the forwarding controller, move there with their family).
  They are checked verbatim by the same script.
* **Spec theorems and supporting lemmas** are new public statements, inserted in the home file
  before the first row they serve. A spec whose proof needs a private lemma of its home file is
  `sorry` here, under a proof sketch that names the existing proof it comes from; a spec whose
  proof needs only public declarations is proved here, and lands with that proof.
* **Row corollaries** `MIG1Gate.row_X` are stated as `type_of% @X`, the landed row's own type,
  so this unit elaborates only if every row keeps its statement while becoming a corollary of
  the specs. They are not landed in the statement PR: at the fill stage each row's proof becomes
  the proof given here, and the row's statement, name and home stay as they are. The other
  `MIG1Gate` declarations are evidence too: the two head lemmas that move from Catalog to
  Simulation, and the two retired canonical rows re-derived as their consumers will be.

The spec theorems use the library's existing style (`ComputesInTime`, `ComputesFunInTime`,
`spaceUsed` from `initCfg`, `Cfg.ofWords` seams), not `Turing.Contract` instances (user decision
of 2026-10-13; `audits/evidence/mig1/MIG1-design.md` §2). The decision rests on the shape of the
facts (whole-machine runs from `initCfg`, judged by the output, with no exact endpoint) and on the
order of work (a contract needs a named machine, so named witnesses come first, for MIG-11 and
MIG-17); the layering obstacle of design §2, reason 1, lasts only until MIG-0b splits
`Build/Contract.lean` into a core that does not import Catalog.

## Main definitions

* Composition: `idTM`, `constTM`, `ifEqTM`, `condTM`. Wrappers: `timedCondTM`.
  Encoding: `Turing.pairDiagTM`, `toCodeTM`. TimeConstructible: `lengthBitsTM`.
* Loop: `loopHostTM`, `emitLoopTM`, `callTM`, `callEntry`, `callExit`.
* Primitives: `prependTM`, `incFixedTM`, `pairValidTM`, `pairExtractTM`, `polyUnaryTM`,
  `polyBitsTM`, `pairLenCheckTM`, `stripLastTM`, `pairMapSndTM`, `splitSolveTM`,
  `splitSolveWithTM`, `unaryTokenTM`, `appendBitTM`.

## Main results

* The generic run lemmas `Turing.MultiTapeTM.abs_workTapePos_runFrom_sub_le` and
  `Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.spaceUsed_le` (proved), and the canonical-word endpoint lemmas
  `Turing.Cfg.ofWords_copy_endpoint`, `Turing.Cfg.ofWords_transfer_endpoint` (proved).
* One time spec per witness, a space spec for the witnesses with their own space argument,
  and the configuration-level contracts of the loop host and the clean call.
* The 53 rows, `Complexity.timeConstructible_id` and `Turing.FinTM.redirectTM_spaceUsedByTape`
  as `MIG1Gate.row_*` corollaries.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.2: the machine model and its basic routines; §1.3:
  time constructibility; Definition 4.1: the visited-cells space measure.)
-/

## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/parts/01-Simulation.lean.txt =====

/-! ════ Part 1. `TuringMachine/Simulation.lean`: the generic run lemmas, the branch union's
space, and the two head lemmas moved from Catalog. -/
-- @landing TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Simulation
-- @imports TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Simulation

namespace Turing.MultiTapeTM

/-- **Head displacement along a run** (landing:
`Turing.MultiTapeTM.abs_workTapePos_runFrom_sub_le`, new in `TuringMachine/Simulation.lean`,
namespace `Turing.MultiTapeTM`; statement and proof verbatim from the H2 statement-gate draft
`audits/evidence/h2/StepBlockDraft.lean.txt:729`, whose proof is `CodeSimulator`'s private
`h1Run_headBound`). After `t` steps of any machine, every work head is within `t` cells of where
it started: the run form of `Turing.MultiTapeTM.workTapePos_step_le`. [AB09, §1.2: a step moves
each head by at most one cell.] One lemma serves MIG-1, where it replaces Catalog's private
`f2_head_steps` (the same fact as two inequalities, retired with MIG-1 by backlog F6-1(g)), and
H2, whose design note O9 moves it below `Build/StepBlock.lean` with MIG-1. Whichever of the two
PRs lands first introduces it; the other cites it.

**Proof sketch.** Telescope the displacement into its `t` one-step differences; the triangle
inequality and the one-step bound give `t`. -/
-- @@verbatim H2Draft - --public --nodoc abs_workTapePos_runFrom_sub_le

end Turing.MultiTapeTM

namespace Turing.FinTM

/-- **Space from time** (landing: `Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.spaceUsed_le`, new in
`TuringMachine/Simulation.lean`; statement and proof are Catalog's private `f2_space_of_time`,
moved). If `M` halts on `x` with output `y` within `T` steps, then at every time `t` its work
tapes have visited at most `M.k · (T + 1)` cells in all. [AB09, Definition 4.1, and the remark
opening the proof of Theorem 4.2: a machine running in time `T` visits at most `T + 1` cells of
each tape.]

**Proof sketch.** After the halt the configuration no longer changes, so every head position at
any time `t` already occurs at some time `u ≤ T`. Each tape's visited set is therefore contained
in the image of `{0, …, T}`, which has at most `T + 1` elements; sum over the `k` tapes. -/
-- @@verbatim Catalog Space --public --nodoc f2_space_of_time

/-- **The branch union's space** (landing: `Turing.FinTM.branchTM_spaceUsed`, new in
`TuringMachine/Simulation.lean` after `branchTM_computes`; statement verbatim from Catalog's
private `f2_branch_space`, whose proof moves with it). The branch union selecting `b` uses
exactly the selected machine's space plus one origin cell for each tape of the idle bank.

**Proof sketch.** Catalog's `f2_branch_space`: the branch union runs the selected machine on its
own bank (`leftCfg_run`, `rightCfg_run`) and never moves the other bank's heads, whose visited
sets stay the origin singletons; split the sum over the two banks with `Fin.sum_univ_add`, which
replaces the copied `f2_sum_add`. -/
-- @@verbatim Catalog Branch --public --nodoc --stmt f2_branch_space

namespace MIG1Gate

/-- **Moved head lemma** (landing: `Turing.FinTM.rewind_scan_heads`, moved verbatim, name and
statement unchanged, from `Build/Catalog.lean:10376` to `TuringMachine/Simulation.lean` after
`Turing.FinTM.timed_rewind`; here inside `MIG1Gate` to avoid the clash with the Catalog
original). A native input rewind keeps every work head fixed, at every prefix, including its
dispatch step.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on the input position; each step is a `controlAction`. -/
-- @@verbatim Catalog - --nodoc rewind_scan_heads

/-- **Moved head lemma** (landing: `Turing.FinTM.rewind_heads`, moved verbatim from
`Build/Catalog.lean:10415`, name and statement unchanged; here inside `MIG1Gate`). The bounded
rewind reaches its destination with the input head at `1` within `pos + 2` steps, and every work
head stays put throughout. (Copied verbatim except that one line of 109 characters is wrapped.)

**Proof sketch.** One start step, then `Turing.FinTM.rewind_scan` for the run and
`Turing.FinTM.rewind_scan_heads` for the heads. -/
theorem rewind_heads {k : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
    (tm : MultiTapeTM k Bool S) (start scan : S) (dest : Option S)
    (hstart : ∀ inp work, tm.tr start inp work = controlAction .neg (some scan))
    (hscan : ∀ inp work, tm.tr scan inp work = match inp with
      | some _ => controlAction .neg (some scan)
      | none => controlAction .pos dest)
    (c : Cfg k Bool S x) (hs : c.state = some start) :
    ∃ r ≤ c.inputPos.val + 2,
      tm.runFrom c r = {c with state := dest, inputPos := 1} ∧
      ∀ u ≤ r, (tm.runFrom c u).workTapePos = c.workTapePos := by
  have hstep : tm.step c =
      {c with state := some scan, inputPos := moveInputPos c.inputPos .neg} := by
    simp only [MultiTapeTM.step, hs, hstart, controlAction_apply]
  have hp : (moveInputPos c.inputPos .neg).val ≤ x.length := by
    rw [moveInputPos_neg_val]
    have := c.inputPos.isLt
    omega
  refine ⟨1 + ((moveInputPos c.inputPos .neg).val + 1), ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [moveInputPos_neg_val]; omega
  · rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add]
    change tm.runFrom (tm.step c) _ = _
    rw [hstep, rewind_scan tm scan dest hscan _ rfl hp]
  · intro u hu
    cases u with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ u =>
      rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, hstep]
      exact rewind_scan_heads tm scan dest hscan (moveInputPos c.inputPos .neg).val _ rfl rfl hp u
        (by omega)

end MIG1Gate

end Turing.FinTM

## ===== audits/evidence/mig1/gate/parts/02-Composition.lean.txt =====

/-! ════ Part 2. `TuringMachine/Composition.lean`: the copy, constant, comparison and
conditional machines, the buffered composition's specs, and the seven rows. -/
-- @landing TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Composition
-- @imports TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Composition
-- @imports TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Simulation

namespace Turing.FinTM

/-- **The copy machine** (landing: `Turing.FinTM.idTM`, made public in place at
`TuringMachine/Composition.lean:88`, body unchanged). A machine with no work tapes and one state
that writes each input symbol to its output while moving right, and halts on the blank after
the input. [AB09, §1.2] -/
-- @@verbatim Composition - --public --nodoc idTM

/-- **The copy machine's time** (landing: `Turing.FinTM.idTM_computes`, new in `Composition`
before `computesFunInTime_id`). On every input `x` the copy machine halts within `|x| + 1`
steps with output `x`. [AB09, §1.2]

**Proof sketch.** The body of today's `computesFunInTime_id` (`Composition.lean:137`) up to its
final weakening: by the private run invariant `idTM_run`, after `|x|` steps the machine is live,
its input head is at cell `|x| + 1` and it has written `x`; there it reads the blank, and the
next step halts without writing. -/
theorem idTM_computes (x : List Bool) : idTM.ComputesInTime x x (x.length + 1) := by
  sorry

/-- **The constant machine** (landing: `Turing.FinTM.constTM`, made public in place at
`Composition.lean:168`, body unchanged). A machine with no work tapes whose `|w| + 1` states
form the emission chain of the fixed word `w`: it writes `w`, one symbol per step, ignoring its
input, and halts. [AB09, §1.2] -/
-- @@verbatim Composition - --public --nodoc constTM

/-- **The constant machine's time** (landing: `Turing.FinTM.constTM_computes`, new in
`Composition` before `computesFunInTime_const`; proved, the row's body moved). On every input
the constant machine halts within `|w| + 1` steps with output `w`. [AB09, §1.2]

**Proof sketch.** The emission chain writes `w` in `|w|` steps and halts on the next
(`Turing.FinTM.emit_halts`), appending to the initially empty output. -/
theorem constTM_computes (w x : List Bool) :
    (constTM w).ComputesInTime x w (w.length + 1) := by
  obtain ⟨hs, ho⟩ := emit_halts (constTM w).tm w id (fun _ _ _ => rfl)
    ((constTM w).tm.initCfg x) rfl
  exact ⟨_, hs, by simpa only [MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Cfg.init, List.nil_append] using ho, rfl⟩

/-- **The fixed-word comparator** (landing: `Turing.FinTM.ifEqTM`, made public in place at
`Composition.lean:189`, body unchanged). A machine with no work tapes that compares its input
with the fixed word `w₀` symbol by symbol and then runs the emission chain of `u` (on an exact
match followed by the blank) or of `v` (on the first mismatch, an early blank, or a symbol past
the end of `w₀`). [AB09, §1.2] -/
-- @@verbatim Composition - --public --nodoc ifEqTM

/-- **The comparator's time** (landing: `Turing.FinTM.ifEqTM_computes`, new in `Composition`
before `computesFunInTime_ifEq`). The comparator computes `w ↦ if w = w₀ then u else v` within
`(|w₀| + max |u| |v| + 3)·(n + 1)` steps, the constant of today's row made explicit.

**Proof sketch.** The body of today's `computesFunInTime_ifEq` (`Composition.lean:335`): the
private comparison run `ifEq_run` reaches the halt within `|w₀| + max |u| |v| + 3` steps with
the selected word as output, and that constant is at most its product with `n + 1`. -/
theorem ifEqTM_computes (w₀ u v : List Bool) :
    (ifEqTM w₀ u v).ComputesFunInTime (fun w => if w = w₀ then u else v)
      (fun n => (w₀.length + max u.length v.length + 3) * (n + 1)) := by
  sorry

/-- **The buffered composition computes the composite** (landing:
`Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM_computesFunInTime`, new in `Composition` before
`computesFunInTime_comp`; proved, the row's body moved). If `M₁` computes `f` within `T₁` and
`M₂` computes `g` within a monotone `T₂`, then `bufferedCompTM M₁ M₂` computes `g ∘ f` within
`2·(T₁ n + T₂ (T₁ n) + 1)` steps. [AB09, §1.2; the composition that [AB09] leaves to
high-level descriptions.]

**Proof sketch.** `bufferedCompTM_computesInTime` gives `T₁ |x| + |f x| + 2 + T₂ |f x|`; the
intermediate word is no longer than the time that produced it (`output_length_le`), and
monotonicity of `T₂` turns `T₂ |f x|` into `T₂ (T₁ |x|)`. -/
theorem bufferedCompTM_computesFunInTime {M₁ M₂ : FinTM Bool} {f g : List Bool → List Bool}
    {T₁ T₂ : ℕ → ℕ}
    (h₁ : M₁.ComputesFunInTime f T₁) (h₂ : M₂.ComputesFunInTime g T₂)
    (hT₂ : Monotone T₂) :
    (bufferedCompTM M₁ M₂).ComputesFunInTime (g ∘ f) fun n => 2 * (T₁ n + T₂ (T₁ n) + 1) := by
  intro x
  have hlen : (f x).length ≤ T₁ x.length := by
    have ho := ((computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mp (h₁ x)).2
    simpa only [ho] using M₁.tm.output_length_le x (T₁ x.length)
  have htime : T₂ (f x).length ≤ T₂ (T₁ x.length) := hT₂ hlen
  exact (bufferedCompTM_computesInTime M₁ M₂ (h₁ x) (h₂ (f x))).mono
    (by dsimp only; omega)

/-- **The buffered composition on the first machine's image** (landing:
`Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM_computesFunInTime_on_image`, new in `Composition` before
`exists_comp_on_image`; proved, the row's body moved). If `M` computes `f` within `T₁` and, for
every input `x`, `U` maps `f x` to `g x` within `T₂ |x|` steps, then `bufferedCompTM M U`
computes `g` within `2·T₁ n + T₂ n + 2` steps. No totality of `U` and no monotonicity is
assumed.

**Proof sketch.** As `bufferedCompTM_computesFunInTime`, with the second phase's budget
measured at the original input length. -/
theorem bufferedCompTM_computesFunInTime_on_image (M U : FinTM Bool)
    (f g : List Bool → List Bool) (T₁ T₂ : ℕ → ℕ) (hM : M.ComputesFunInTime f T₁)
    (hU : ∀ x, U.ComputesInTime (f x) (g x) (T₂ x.length)) :
    (bufferedCompTM M U).ComputesFunInTime g (fun n => 2 * T₁ n + T₂ n + 2) := by
  intro x
  have hlen : (f x).length ≤ T₁ x.length := by
    have ho := ((computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mp (hM x)).2
    simpa only [ho] using M.tm.output_length_le x (T₁ x.length)
  exact (bufferedCompTM_computesInTime M U (hM x) (hU x)).mono (by dsimp only; omega)

/-- **The buffered composition's halting relation** (landing:
`Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM_computes_iff`, new in `Composition` before `exists_comp_partial`;
proved, the row's body moved). For all machines `M₁`, `M₂` and words `x`, `w`: the buffered
composition halts on `x` with output `w` if and only if `M₁` halts on `x` with some output `y`
and `M₂` halts on `y` with output `w`. No totality or time hypotheses.

**Proof sketch.** The body of today's `exists_comp_partial` (`Composition.lean:474`): a
divergent first phase keeps every composite configuration live (`bufferedFirstCfg_run`);
otherwise `bufferedComp_start` reaches the second phase with `M₂`'s initial configuration on the
virtual input `y`, and `bufferedSecondCfg_run` tracks `M₂` step for step in both directions. -/
theorem bufferedCompTM_computes_iff (M₁ M₂ : FinTM Bool) (x w : List Bool) :
    (∃ t, (bufferedCompTM M₁ M₂).ComputesInTime x w t) ↔
      ∃ y : List Bool, (∃ t, M₁.ComputesInTime x y t) ∧ ∃ t, M₂.ComputesInTime y w t := by
  classical
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨t, ht⟩
    -- A divergent first component would keep every composite configuration live.
    have hh : ∃ s, (M₁.tm.runFrom (M₁.tm.initCfg x) s).state = none := by
      by_contra h
      have hr := bufferedFirstCfg_run M₁ M₂ (M₁.tm.initCfg x) t
        (fun s _ hs => h ⟨s, hs⟩)
      rw [← bufferedFirstCfg_init] at hr
      have hc := ((computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mp ht).1
      rw [hr] at hc
      simp only [bufferedFirstCfg, Option.some_ne_none] at hc
    obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := hh
    let y := (M₁.tm.runFrom (M₁.tm.initCfg x) s).output
    have hy : M₁.ComputesInTime x y s := (computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mpr ⟨hs, rfl⟩
    obtain ⟨a, p, tapes, heads, _, ha⟩ := bufferedComp_start M₁ M₂ x y s hy
    -- Extend a completed run past the verified administrative prefix.
    have hc := (computesInTime_iff _ x w (a + t)).mp (ht.mono (by omega))
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, ha] at hc
    obtain ⟨b, _, hr⟩ := bufferedSecondCfg_run M₁ M₂ (M₂.tm.initCfg y) true
      (by simp [VirtualTag, MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Cfg.init]) p tapes heads t
    rw [hr] at hc
    refine ⟨y, ⟨s, hy⟩, t, (computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mpr ?_⟩
    exact ⟨by simpa only [bufferedSecondCfg, Option.map_eq_none_iff] using hc.1, hc.2⟩
  · rintro ⟨y, ⟨s, hs⟩, ⟨t, ht⟩⟩
    obtain ⟨a, p, tapes, heads, _, ha⟩ := bufferedComp_start M₁ M₂ x y s hs
    obtain ⟨b, _, hr⟩ := bufferedSecondCfg_run M₁ M₂ (M₂.tm.initCfg y) true
      (by simp [VirtualTag, MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Cfg.init]) p tapes heads t
    have hc := (computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mp ht
    refine ⟨a + t, (computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mpr ?_⟩
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, ha, hr]
    exact ⟨by simpa only [bufferedSecondCfg, Option.map_eq_none_iff] using hc.1, hc.2⟩

/-- **The untimed conditional** (landing: `Turing.FinTM.condTM`, made public in place at
`Composition.lean:517`, body unchanged). Run `D` with its first emission captured in a state
register, rewind the input, then enter `M₁` or `M₂` on disjoint fresh tapes according to the
register; an empty register at dispatch halts. -/
-- @@verbatim Composition - --public --nodoc condTM

/-- **The untimed conditional's halting relation** (landing: `Turing.FinTM.condTM_computes_iff`,
new in `Composition` before `exists_cond`). If `D` computes `x ↦ [p x]`, then on every input
`x` the conditional halts with output `w` if and only if the branch `cond (p x) M₁ M₂` halts on
`x` with output `w`.

**Proof sketch.** The body of today's `exists_cond` (`Composition.lean:654`): the private
`condTM_start` reaches the selected branch's initial configuration, after which `rightCfg_run`
tracks the branch union step for step and `branchTM_computes` identifies the selected branch. -/
theorem condTM_computes_iff (D M₁ M₂ : FinTM Bool) (p : List Bool → Bool)
    (hD : D.Computes fun x => [p x]) (x w : List Bool) :
    (∃ t, (condTM D M₁ M₂).ComputesInTime x w t) ↔
      ∃ t, (cond (p x) M₁ M₂).ComputesInTime x w t := by
  sorry

/-- **Row** `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_id`, statement unchanged. -/
theorem MIG1Gate.row_computesFunInTime_id : type_of% @Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_id :=
  ⟨idTM, 1, fun x => (idTM_computes x).mono (by simp)⟩

/-- **Row** `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_const`, statement unchanged. -/
theorem MIG1Gate.row_computesFunInTime_const :
    type_of% @Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_const :=
  fun w => ⟨constTM w, w.length + 1, fun x =>
    (constTM_computes w x).mono (Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (Nat.succ_pos _))⟩

/-- **Row** `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_ifEq`, statement unchanged. -/
theorem MIG1Gate.row_computesFunInTime_ifEq : type_of% @Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_ifEq :=
  fun w₀ u v => ⟨ifEqTM w₀ u v, _, ifEqTM_computes w₀ u v⟩

/-- **Row** `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_comp`, statement unchanged. -/
theorem MIG1Gate.row_computesFunInTime_comp : type_of% @Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_comp :=
  fun h₁ h₂ hT₂ => ⟨_, 2, bufferedCompTM_computesFunInTime h₁ h₂ hT₂⟩

/-- **Row** `Turing.FinTM.exists_comp_on_image`, statement unchanged. -/
theorem MIG1Gate.row_exists_comp_on_image : type_of% @Turing.FinTM.exists_comp_on_image :=
  fun M U f g T₁ T₂ hM hU => ⟨_, bufferedCompTM_computesFunInTime_on_image M U f g T₁ T₂ hM hU⟩

/-- **Row** `Turing.FinTM.exists_comp_partial`, statement unchanged. -/
theorem MIG1Gate.row_exists_comp_partial : type_of% @Turing.FinTM.exists_comp_partial :=
  fun M₁ M₂ => ⟨bufferedCompTM M₁ M₂, bufferedCompTM_computes_iff M₁ M₂⟩

/-- **Row** `Turing.FinTM.exists_cond`, statement unchanged. -/
theorem MIG1Gate.row_exists_cond : type_of% @Turing.FinTM.exists_cond :=
  fun D M₁ M₂ p hD => ⟨condTM D M₁ M₂, condTM_computes_iff D M₁ M₂ p hD⟩
